In the so-called civilized kingdoms of Hyboria, nobles build great palaces with walls of mighty stone to protect themselves from their enemies at court and abroad. The solution to sturdy walls and cowardly nobility is the steadfast trebuchet. A machine of immense power, the trebuchet can hurl stones, corpses, and even specially designed explosives.

Their weakness is immobility. Once placed, they cannot be easily moved, and finding the correct range and angle requires time and patience. With repeated use, it is almost certain that some or all of the components of the trebuchet will degrade and need to be replaced.

These projectiles of smelted iron are sure to pulverize flesh, bone, and stone.

This armor set bears the symbols and iconography of a lost age. Neither its colors nor styling corresponds to any known kingdom or military formation of the Hyborian Age. The pinnacle of protection, this great helm is a solid wall of defense against any type of attack, but the extreme weight requirements mean that the wearer must sacrifice mobility.

A scout saddle in the Aquilonian style

Aquilonia has a long tradition with horse-riding and cavalry. With the province of Poitain in the south is well known for its armored cavalry. Bored nobles often amuse themselves with jousting tournaments where knights hurl themselves at one another time and again in the lists.

This saddle is specially designed for scouting. It is light, easy to fit, and allows the horse good freedom of movement. This means that the horse can run further without becoming tired, can turn quickly when danger approaches and has a good amount of speed. It won't win any races and it is definitely not a saddle designed to withstand any kind of battle.
A cavalry saddle designed to intimidate

Where Aquilonia borders upon the Pictish Wilderness, life is brutal, harsh and often short. The Pictish raids upon Aquilonian forts are brutal affairs and settlers who have come west seeking their fortune often lose everything.

Because of the density of the jungle and the difficult terrain, cavalry is almost always out of the question. However, one exception are the messengers who travel along the roads between the forts and the settlements. As a primary target for Pictish raiders, these men and women are among the most hardy along the frontier, and they decorate their saddles with bone ornaments to scare off the superstitious Picts.

Though the style varies from culture to culture, the cavalry saddle shares several elements across the board. It is designed to allow horses the mobility they need to accelerate as fast as possible. Though not capable of being sustained for a long time, the cavalry saddle also allows horses to reach their greatest speed potential.

The Exiled Lands has no tradition in riding. The terrain is downright unfriendly to horses and the beasts themselves have no natural presence here. However, due to sheer-minded persistence and strong will, horses have been tamed and brought to the Exiled Lands. A testament and a congratulations to all who suffered to make this happen.

Some types of cavalry rely on their speed and mobility to perform flanking Maneuvers, while others are all about the charge. This saddle is designed for the latter - allowing attackers to stay in the stirrups taking repeated blows while they use the momentum of their mounts to force a break in enemy lines. For anyone who wishes to ride a mount into battle and stay there for a while, this is the saddle of choice.

Saddle, stirrups, and other riding gear necessary to train, ride, and hitch horses

South of the Pictish Wilderness is the Valley of Zingg, a fertile plain of rolling hillocks and valleys that is home to a breed of wild horses prized for their strength and fierceness. As the region evolved into what would become modern Zingara, the nobility of the Kordavan capital enacted laws to protect the bloodlines of the Kordavan stallion from adulteration. The renowned Kordavan tack and saddle has a larger contact area than typical saddles and is suitable for many hours of riding.

The swift-footed Picts would run them down within a mile, unless - he took his position behind a tangle of fallen logs beside the trail. A long, pole-like weapon with a sharpened end

<LoreItalics> There were the knights, gleaming in richly wrought plate-armor, colored plumes waving above their burnished sallets. Their steeds, caparisoned with silk, lacquered leather and gold buckles, caracoled and curvetted as their riders put them through their paces. The early light struck glints from lance-points that rose like a forest above the array, their pennons flowing in the breeze.</> - Black Colossus

Lances are the shock weapon of the cavalry charge and they have the ability to break armies at the first engagement.
Despite being heavy and unwieldy, lances are always the first choice of weapon for cavalry (with the exception of the uniquely talented Hyrkanian horse archers).

True bravery is the ability to stand and face a cavalry charge - a bristling forest of lances being driven towards the line by hard-faced men on screaming horses.

Lances rarely survive first contact, breaking or splintering or being lodged through the chest of a foe. Most cavalry carry a secondary weapon into battle for this reason.

A throne made of corrupted stone

Unlike other chairs, a throne gives the one who sits in it authority above and beyond that of an ordinary man.
Battles have always been fought for this kind of power, and they always will be.
Sitting on a throne of any kind will increase confidence and prowess for a period.

The favored choice of many mean drunks, these shards can do serious damage when poked into the soft bits of your opponent.
Reinforced with a star metal core, this weapon may look improvised but in fact is nothing more than a solid metal stick made to look innocuous.
A mad cook from Zingara once sharpened his spatula to a fine, flesh-tearing tool of destruction in order to guarantee total customer satisfaction.
Rigor mortis has set in a long time ago

<LoreItalics>Conan brained him with the beef bone, took his poniard and his keys, and made a leisurely departure.</> - Rogues in the House

This leg, severed from the corpse of an enemy, is bloodless and stiff. Carrying it around might not be a good way to make friends, but then again it might help to make a different kind of friend.
The important thing is that it can be used as a weapon. And beating someone to death with a limb is an itch that rarely gets scratched in civilized society.

A star metal shovel that has been outfitted with a sturdy grip and sharpened. It serves the dual function of both killing your opponent and using it to dig their grave.

Most humble of materials and most common, stone is the building block of civilization. From the primitive weapons of Picts to the marble sheathed palaces of Aquilonian Kings, stone is the foundation upon which all is predicated.
A queen bee used for producing honey

<LoreItalics>Our wisdom flows so sweet. Taste and see.</> - The Buzzing
Beehives pulse with activity and life - and at the beating heart of the hive is the queen bee. Usually the mother of all the bees in the hive - without her the hive would no longer produce honey.

<LoreItalics>Our wisdom flows so sweet. Taste and see.</> - The Buzzing
They give their lives to the hive, and the hive gives honey to those who take it. This is perhaps, a metaphor for kingdoms and those who plunder them.
Or simply the lives of bees.
Strip of bark torn from a tree

Strip of bark torn from a tree. Use for tanning leather and as a meagre fuel source. A byproduct of using bark in the tanning process is Tar.
The leatherworkers of Kordava are renowned for their supple and pliant leather. Their process for tanning, and the bark that they use, is a well-guarded secret.
Teas brewed from the bark of certain trees are rumoured to cure many different kinds of ailment.

Readily available and easily shaped with the right tools, wood is ubiquitous in the weapons and buildings of primitive tribes and mighty nations.  
Wood allows for the creation of fire and its easy transport.
A sturdy branch fallen from a tree
Branches can be used to create rudimentary weapons and tools, which can then be used to shape wood for more beneficial purposes.

Bone is not particularly durable and will shatter easily upon iron or steel.

Through the long passage of eons, rumors of dragons have always been passed down from generation to generation, and the legacy of these fearsome creatures grows with each telling.

The sad reality of dragons was that they could not fly, they did not breathe fire or acid, and they were not particularly intelligent. They were simply gigantic predators that lived centuries ago.

Through their arts, the Giant-kings resurrected dragons from the bones that they could find. They kept them as pets and bred them for battle in their gladiatorial games. 

Their bones are particularly strong and can be worked into powerful weapons.

A weighted club for knocking out foes

This truncheon once belonged to Jin-Zhao the Tiger, the leader of a ruthless slave-trader band. His legacy is not written upon scrolls or stones but endures in the traumatized memories of those who lost loved ones to his club's skull-crushing infamy.

Born a slave, Jin-Zhao claimed his fearsome title in the blood-soaked fighting pits of Khitai. There, amidst the roars and jeers of the bloodthirsty crowd, he battled a tiger as fierce as the emperor's wrath, wild and relentless. The fight left Jin-Zhao victorious but marked by the beast's claws in ragged lines that strangely evoked the tiger's own stripes and forever proclaimed his ferocity.

If asked whether it is better to be loved or feared, Jin-Zhao would undoubtedly choose fear, for in the harsh lands of Khitai, fear serves as the sharpest weapon.

Ropes have dozens of uses, but most common in the Exiled Lands is the binding and capture of thralls. Once an enemy is rendered unconscious, their ankles are bound with rope and they are dragged into captivity.

Made through an esoteric and life-threatening process of curing the knotted lengths of the hair of the deceased in highly venomous fermented tree sap, this rope may be the last one you ever need.

No man trusts his fellow and the true statesmen dare not speak to each other what is in the minds of all.</> - The Shadow Kingdom

Some humans are traitors to their kind. When the Elder races ruled the earth, these men and women willingly worked for the enemy, in return for better conditions for them and their families.
Often, they were used as guardians on the sacrificial temples. Upon these blood-soaked altars, the Guardians held sway as symbols of sheer terror.

Any human mustering the courage to defy the Elders suffered the wrath of a Guardian's Will Breaker. A blow of this hammer pulverizes bone, reducing a body to a leaking sack of jellied flesh. Limbs flail and slump as the victim suffers the most grevious pinch of their swiftly-ending life.

It was used to transport heavy loads of prisoners, soldiers, or goods between the cities and outposts of the empire in his name. However, without beasts in yoke, the cart holds fast where it was abandoned, diminishing the advance of the empire along with it.
A large basin to hold the skulls of fallen sorcerers

Typically, a basin of this design would hold water, display goods, or showcase treasures. However, this grim pedestal served a far more sinister purpose for the Khitan exiles. It was used to collect the skulls of Kurak's acolytes and display them as macabre wards to defend their outposts. These skulls were destined to find their way to Mek-Kamoses, who sought to unravel the mysteries of sorcery in the Exiled Lands.
An explosive payload designed for celebration instead of destruction

When ignited, they burst into the night sky with a brilliant array of lights and sounds, reminiscent of the grand festivals in far-off Khitai. Beyond their beauty, these fireworks serve as a symbol of hope and celebration, bringing a moment of joy and wonder to the otherwise unforgiving Exiled Lands. Use them to signal allies, celebrate victories, or simply to light up the darkness with the splendor of Khitai.

Like cultures and customs, the value of ivory depends upon the kingdom where it is seen.

In the Hyborian kingdoms, where elephants and other creatures are rare, it is a tangible sign of both wealth and power. In the Black Kingdoms, it is common - few warriors exist in those lands who do not possess an ivory handled dagger or jewelry.

It is a great source of trade between the north and the south - indeed it could be said that ivory is the primary reason that merchants dare make the dangerous journey along the Black Coast to trade for it in Kush.

The great herds of elephants which roam the Black Kingdoms are hunted daily for their tusks and there is no reason for men to suspect that the creatures will not continue to roam forever.

Hopefully it was dead, otherwise, somewhere out there in the wilderness there is a panther struggling frantically to maintain its grip on a tree, a bear casually slapping a deer on the rump or a very confused pack of wolves sliding across an icy lake.

Claws can be ground into bone meal in a Grinder.

There was one attempt, years past, to make an independent currency built around the principles of free exchange and free markets. Unfortunately, the necromancer who invented the idea was executed before it could take root and his crypt-o-currency was forgotten.

A handful of odorous, yet powerful, matter

A mixture of fine and coarse bone grindings

A non-descript tome, worn with age and use. Easily overlooked by the untrained eye, the book is a gateway to a new reality for those with the proper insight. A reality where the basic spells contained within can alter the very fabric of time and space.
A faded page to be added to the tome

Rare is the spellbook that is conceived, written, and completed. More often than not, the tome begins life as a nearly empty folio with a few basic spells inscribed within. Then, as new spells and rituals are learned, pages are added, and the book becomes something more - a portable archive of arcane knowledge and power. Written in blood as black as the night, this page may also be dismantled for it's precious ink.
A crumpled page containing a failed spell

This work is the product of a rushed, or incompetent sorcerer with an imperfect understanding of the spell they were trying to articulate. Written in blood as black as the night, this page may also be dismantled for it's precious ink.
The hand-drawn map of a dead sorcerer

A navigational tool with a delicately balanced iron needle that always points north. This clever contraption serves as a guiding star through this inhospitable land when the night sky is absent.
Contains various rewards for your efforts.
This package is full of valuable coins and alchemical components - it was a reward for a dangerous request from a vile man.

This bulky package contains a generous reward that may yield rare coins, alchemical reagents, or shaped golem components.
A master key to unlock prisoner cages.
A pitted and well-worn key of hardened steel. Neither the fabrication nor the design of the key is remarkable other than the freedom they imply.
A black heart cut from a Grey One

The hearts of the Grey Ones resemble human hearts, but streaked with a darkness that is as alien as the beings themselves. What purpose such a heart has is difficult to determine. But as the old proverb says - 'a heart in the hand is worth two in the chests of immutable alien foes'.
These scraps are not useful for anything except for being smelted in a furnace.

Recovered from a vault and reforged with hardened steel, this is the closest approximation to the vault materials that it is possible to make.

It is almost alien in its qualities, being easier to work than steel and yet harder than any other substance found in the natural world.

This decayed chunk of metal was recovered from the interior of one of the vaults on the Isle of Siptah. The origin and construction of this metal is unknown and the secret of its smithing has long been forgotten. 

With the right process, however, it is possible to salvage useable metal from this decayed piece.
A chunk of stone pulsing with corruption
Thousands of years of sorcerous rituals have left their essence embedded deeply in this stone. It seethes with dark intent - but perhaps that can be useful.
Basic iron ingot for crude metalworking

The ability to work iron is a step along the road from savagery to civilization. The streets of the great cities of the world resound with the ring of hammer on anvil a song to the march of progress.
Iron weapons and armor offer superior protection, but the additional weight means carrying less supplies.
Iron can be treated with Steelfire in a Furnace to produce steel.
An alloy that is stronger and less brittle than iron

Barring some enchantment, steel is the strongest metal alloy available for the construction of weapons. The crafting of steel requires iron and Steelfire, a peculiar additive made from Tar and Brimstone.
The smiths of Akbitana in Shem are the finest in the world and a weapon made of Akbitanan steel is considered to be unbreakable. Due to their great demand, it is rare to find an Akbitanan weapon outside of Shem.
A nasty yellow substance that corrodes anything it touches

<LoreItalics>You will go into the acid vats along with Thak and the nationalist fools, and none will be the wiser..</> - Rogues in the House

The alchemists of Argos have long known of the existence of the humors, which they say dictate the health of men. This pus-coloured substance retrieved from from the stomach of a ghoul, might well be an example of ghoulish humors. 

It is extremely corrosive to flesh and bone - and can be used to create ichor.
Toxin gland taken from the monstrous scorpion queen
The most potent venom in the Exiled Lands, carefully extracted from the venom glands of the Scorpion Queen.
A leather purse jingling with coin

<LoreItalics>He looked the part of the hired fighting-man, who had known all vicissitudes of fortune, plunder and wealth one day, an empty purse and a close-drawn belt the next..</> - The Hour of the Dragon

This simply leather purse has a nice heft to it and clearly contains a number of coins. How many and of which denomination can only be determined by opening it.
A bag that contains the very basics for survival
This bag contains a bedroll, waterskin, and various other items useful for surviving the harsh climates of these Lands.
This bag contains an assortment of dyes.
Brittle and breakable, glass is best used for ornamentation

Only the wealthy can afford to ornament their houses in glass, even though creating glass is a simple process. Glass offers protection from the elements and a view of what is occurring outside, at the risk of being easily shattered.
Assorted stalks, leaves and sprigs torn from plants

The most basic materials that can be gathered by hand from plants. These fibers can be woven into rough clothing, but it will only provide simple protection against the elements.
Anything woven from such crude material cannot be expected to stop a swinging blade.
Spider silk - soft, strong and lightweight

Harvested from the webs of spiders, gossamer can be spun into a durable, strong thread.
Gathering gossamer would require weeks were it not for the presence of extremely large spiders in the Exiled Lands. Their webs are large enough that gossamer gathering can be a profitable enterprise.
It is not known what causes the spider in the region to grow to such an extreme size, but enterprising Stygians have been harvesting gossamer here for centuries.
The untreated skin of a beast
Taken from any number of wild beasts, hide can be processed into leather using a tannery.
Some creatures have thicker skins than others

Large beasts have developed thicker skins for defence against predators. This thickened skin, while harder to work, provides a superior leather. 
Worshippers of the beast-god, Jhebbal Sag have been known to clothe themselves in the hides of ferocious predators as a symbol of their pact.

Along the reaches of the Styx, the great crocodiles of Stygia are feared as man-eaters and messengers of the gods. Although not as bound to the Stygian religion as the great snakes that haunt the blood-mad streets of Khemi, crocodiles are still revered and considered sacred.
Poachers and hunters from the Black Kingdoms to the south, however, do not share this reverence for the crocodile and willingly hunt them for their skins which make a fine leather.
This reptile skin might have been taken from a crocodile or a large lizard.
Tanned hide that is commonly used for lightweight armors

Supple material that offers enhanced protection. Leather can be stiff and difficult to work if it has not been correctly treated, but there is a fine line between softening the leather too far and having it lose its protective properties.
Leather will help to stop the claws and fangs of a beast, but a determined foe will be able to break through the material.
Used to create armors at an Armorers Bench
Offers a higher degree of protection than regular leather

Offering better protection than regular leather, but at the cost of flexibility.
Thickened leather requires regular oiling to prevent it from becoming inflexible and preventing movement.
Kordavan leather is famed for its pliability and durability, but to learn the secret of its durability would require access to the tanneries of the Zingaran capital.
A strong, light thread spun from gossamer

Silk is a valuable commodity in the Hyborian kingdoms and it flows from Khitai in the east and Stygia in the south. Khitan silk is drawn from silkworms whereas Stygian silk is harvested from the giant spiders that inhabit the dark reaches of the southern lands.
Khitan silk is prized for the clinging, sensual fabric that it creates. It is very tolerant of dyes and holds brilliant color. Any nobleman of note has at least one outfit of Khitan silk.
Stygian silk is stronger and more durable, offering greater protection at the cost of a coarser weave. Dyes tend to fade quickly but the tenacity of the fabric makes it a favorite among the merchant class.
A viscous, foul smelling fluid collected from arthropods

Medicine men and herbalists tend to pay well for the ichors of exotic and dangerous species killed in the wilds, but it has other, hidden properties.
In Stygia, ichor is mixed with fibers and used to harden stone under very high heat, adding a glaze to the stone that makes it impervious to normal weapons.

Raw meat is a dangerous temptation for the starving and desperate. Consuming it provides immediate relief from hunger but at the risk of inheriting any disease or parasite that may have come along for the ride.
This flesh is harvested from small animals. It is not particularly filling or flavorful. 
Unless this meat is cooked quickly, it will spoil and become inedible.
Raw flesh harvested from common wild animals

This flesh has been harvested from large game. It is easy to cook and full of flavour.
Unless this meat is cooked quickly, it will spoil and become inedible.

Unless this meat is cooked quickly, it will spoil and become inedible.
Many eggs, amongst others the Shaleback eggs, are considered a rare delicacy in the civilized lands. Anybody who has seen an enraged adult Shaleback up close can understand why they remain so.
For the strong of stomach, these grubs offer a both food and moisture in the midst of the desert
These will keep starvation at bay. Barely.
To the starving, a handful of insects can be enough to stave off hunger for a while.
A bite sized scorpion snack with extra sting
A hard crunchy shell with a soft, satisfying center. These are considered a delicacy in some cultures.
Small seeds taken from the foilage of the Exiled Lands
These small seeds can be ground into a paste and made into a thin gruel.
The larvae of a Shaggai Horror that grow into pets when cultivated in a beehive with ample honey.
Shaggai self-propagate through the traumatic implantation of larvae into a compatible host. Beehives with active honey producers effectively mimic the conditions necessary for compatibility.
Component innards from a monster necessary in the creation of demon-blood.
This slick, meaty organ is notoriously difficult to harvest intact, but an undamaged vessel can convert normal blood into demon-blood with the help of a fluid press.

Consuming the flesh of men is a mark of savagery and desperation. Various demonic religious practices encourage ritual consumption while some tribes in the Black Kingdoms devour pieces of their fallen enemies in order to absorb their prowess and courage.
The desert men of Darfar are well known for their cannibalism. With their teeth filed to points and bizarre hairstyles of mud and twigs they are an intimidating sight - more so with the blood of a fresh kill drying on their chins.
Eyes taken from a being of pure innocence

It is said that all beings are born with light eyes, that darken when the world begins to stain them. These eyes, taken from a creature too young to know the evils of the world, contain a certain amount of power that can be called upon in occult rituals.

Tough, chewy meat that spoils quickly. Preferential to scavenged foods or raw meat, this gamy meat is hard on the teeth and the palate.
The taverns of the great cities are known using this type of meat for stewing though in Shadizar it is more likely to be cat or rat scraps that find their way into the pot.

Juicy with the blood and fat of the kill, this universally life sustaining meal could as easily be found around the campfires of hunters from Vanaheim to the southern Black Kingdoms.
Flavorful and filling, the only downside is the relative ease with which the meat becomes spoiled.
A cooked haunch of exotic meat

Taken from one of the more unusual beasts of the Exiled Lands, this mouth-watering meat is the height of culinary grace in this savage land.
In the great palaces of the Hyborian kingdoms noblemen hold lavish feasts where the reek of intrigue and exotic meats fill the smoky air. The quests that their servants undertake - and the dangers that they face - to obtain the near-mythical fare is the stuff of epicurean legend.
Made from plant seeds that have been ground into a paste and mixed with water, this thin and watery gruel is probably not enough to sustain an active adventurer. For thralls, however, it serves.
A simple, nutrient-dense mixture that can fuel an army. What it lacks in nuanced flavor, it makes up for by being both portable and nourishing.
The crushed bones and marrow of an otherworldly creature.

Taken from a dark creature summoned from the outer void, this ground up hunk of disgusting matter glows with an otherworldy energy.
It's probably useful for something, but eating it should be a last resort.
The only thing more disgusting than gruel, is spoiled gruel. This lumpy mixture of mold and clustered clumps of debris should not be eaten. By anything.
A stinking mass of black matter
Whatever this once belonged to, it is now unrecognizable. Any occult properties it may have once possessed are probably expired.
Whatever this used to be, it is inedible now

Meat which has begun to putrefy has an odor and flavour all of its own.
Eating it might stave off starvation, but at the price of becoming violently ill. Even carrion eaters shun putrid meat.
The cooked flesh of the abysmal remnant

This foul-smelling, acidic meat does not look or smell appetizing even after being cooked. Considering the creature that it came from, and the environment where it was found, consuming this would be a foolhardy endeavor.
An offering to the bloody spectacle of battle

Thousands of years past, when the Giant-kings ruled the land and the arena was active, there was a human gladiator named Tyros.
Tyros was a fighter such as the world had never seen - legend had it that he was a descendant of the legendary Kull of Atlantis.
One of the many names that were ascribed to Tyros during his gladiatorial career was that of Dragonslayer. It was said that the appearance of Tyros in the arena was enough to drive the beasts wild with rage. This offering, however, was the more likely cause. Before every battle it was burned on the sacrifice altar and the smoke from the offering was said to drive any within the arena into a mighty frenzy - perhaps even reaching across the boundary between life and death.
This spiky plant has well known healing properties when made into a potion
A favorite of herbalists the world over, the leaves of this plant are highly sought after for their medicinal properties.
Venom swollen glands harvested from serpents

The serpents of the Exiled Lands vary in the potency of their venom from mildly irritating to lethal. 
The use of serpent venom for coating weapons before battle is a myth. Venom needs to be injected directly into the blood to have an effect and the act of plunging a weapon into a body is a far more efficient way to damage foes than to wait for a slow acting venom.
Alchemists and healers, however, do tout the efficacy of ingesting small amounts of venom to build an immunity. It is said that King Yezdigerd of Turan ritually ingests small amounts of many different poisons to build his protection against assassination attempts.
Toxin gland taken from the monstrous reaper

The Sand Reapers spit a venomous toxin that causes the skin to rot from the body on contact. Harvesting this toxin is a foolhardy but valuable undertaking.
Applying this toxin to specially prepared grooved blades allows precise delivery of the toxin to enemies in melee.

Brimstone is one of the most sought after alchemical components due its application in a wide variety of concoctions.
Searing fumes make collecting it a difficult task and the bleached bones of those who did not adequately prepare serve as a grisly warning to others.
Combined with sticky tar, brimstone creates steelfire, which is a catalyst that hardens iron into steel.
Thick black substance used for sealing wood

Prized by alchemists and sailors alike, tar is a black oily substance derived from the dry heating of bark. It is a by-product of using bark in the tanning process.
From the Vilayet to the Western Ocean, shipwrights know the value of tar as a water repellent. The legendary purple-sailed fleet of Turan owes the color to the unusual mix of tar and local chemicals used to soak the sailcloth.
In the gladiatorial arenas of Argos, tar is used to seal cuts and abrasions and ward off minor infections.
A volatile mix of tar and brimstone

An unfortunate smith in Khoraja found himself homeless when his premises burned to the ground. Unable to explain the fire or its root cause, he nevertheless noticed that the steel he had been working on had survived the fire intact and was hardened beyond any metal that he had worked with before.
Being a cautious man, he experimented with different variations of the equipment in his newly rebuilt smithy until he reached the conclusion that tar from his poorly sealed roof had dripped into his bloomery and tainted the brimstone that he was using as a catalyst.
He gave his new catalyst the fanciful name of Steelfire and made a great deal of money before other smiths were able to replicate his results.

Created by twisting lengths of fiber together to create a sturdy length of string, twine is used for binding the most primitive weapons and items together.
The advantage of twine is that it is easily created from scavenged ingredients, such as plant fiber, but it's tendency to unravel at unfortunate times makes anything crafted with it inherently fragile.
Taken from the tresses of dead women

In Zamoria, there was a city ruled by a sorcerer named Yara in his fabulous dwelling known only as the Tower of the Elephant. Yara had a dark reputation, but he was also rumored to be the keeper of a wonderful treasure known only as the Heart of the Elephant.
Nobody knows precisely what happened to Yara, but his tower collapsed into rubble and among the rubble was found a coil of rope woven from hair. Though none knew its purpose, many speculated that the hair for the rope was taken from dead women, in accordance with a ritual found in the dread Book of Skelos, which would make it incredibly strong.
The harvested trunk orb of the Krllyandian.
It's speculated the Krllyandian orb performs a digestive function for the fungoid behemoth. The harvested organ greatly improves the speed at which a compost heap breaks down material.
The harvested hide of the Krllyand.
The thick, fibrous derma of the fungoid Krllyand is host to a diverse ecology of microorganisms that combine to form a remarkably effective fuel for tanneries.
A section of parchment depicting part of a legendary recipe.
The fragment bears script in a faded, energetic hand describing one step in a detailed fabrication process, but the result is unknowable without the associated fragments.
The harvested excretion of a Shaggai Horror.
This milky, white secretion can be used to greatly increase output speed of a beehive and is a vital component to the successful breeding of Shaggai pets.

Those who rob the dead are either desperate, brave or possessed of such dark power that they no longer fear the dead.
The dust stolen from the tombs of dead Stygians is said to cause blindness when flung into the eyes of an opponent. It has darker uses that are detailed in the blasphemous Book of Skelos.
Black liquid that reeks of the outer dark

This black ooze, harvested from the corpse of a demonic entity, steams slightly when exposed to air.
Blood is used to increase the potency of the blasphemous rituals of both priests and sorcerers. And this is particularly potent blood.
The nature of demons is hotly disputed by scholars. Some suggest that they are simply remnants of elder races that stalked the earth before mankind, while others insist that they are formless creatures from the outer void given form by the incantation of vile sorceries.
A volatile powder created by mashing various alchemical components

Alchemists in the west first discovered this wondrous powder through a crumbling manuscript that came with a caravan from Khitai. 
Through much experimentation and loss of limb and life, they eventually stabilized the formula with localized ingredients. Combined with other ingredients, Dragonpowder becomes a potent explosive - though many see it as a form of sorcery and refuse to use it in battle.
A powder crafted from foul ingredients by the Darfari
This powder corrupts absolutely and is used in rituals involving the dead. It can be used to ritually infuse bones in order to raise the dead and corrupt the living.
An eye from the Abysmal Remnant

This eye seems to glow with an inhuman intelligence. The creature from which it was taken was of supernatural origin and this large, almost hypnotic eye explains how it could lure prey close enough to feast.
While the properties of the eye seem to have passed with the death of the creature, it will still make for an impressive trophy.
A fang from the Abysmal Remnant

This fang, harvested from the corpse of the Abysmal Remnant, is made of an extremely hard substance. Due to the acidic environment in which the creature lived the material has developed several properties beyond regular ivory or bone which mean that it is durable.
Flesh harvested from the Abysmal Remnant

This foul-smelling, acidic meat does not look or smell appetizing.
Considering the creature that it came from, and the environment where it was found, consuming this would be a foolhardy endeavor.
A gray flower used to dye clothing
This common flower is used by Hyrkanians to dye their felt yurts.
A plant with flowers of startling color
Cultivated in Stygia, the petals of this plant produce a brightly colored dye which the Stygians use for decorating ceremonial clothing and armor.
Plucked from the bottom of a lake or river, this plant can be used to produce a bright orange dye that sets in even the most stubborn of material.
A small insect with brightly colored innards
These small insects live and feed on cacti. They can be prepared into a bright red dye for use in coloring textiles.

The berries of true mandrake must be taken from the resting place of a dead man by the light of the moon. False mandrake berries are much simpler to harvest and can be used to create a purple dye. 
Some have suggested that the intense blooming of False Mandrake along the banks of the Vilayet during spring is a simple explanation for the fabled purple sails of the Turanian fleet. However, alchemists argue that the purple comes from the properties of the pitch found in the region.
What this is, where it comes from and how it got here are a mystery. What matters is that it can be used in the creation of a cyan dye.
A bile gland taken from a supernatural creature

When the sandstorm comes howling across the Exiled Lands, it is accompanied by the strange screams of the beasts that inhabit it. What they are and why they follow the storms is one of the many mysteries of the Exiled Lands.

<LoreItalics>The tunnel debouched into a wide room before the moonlight played out, an empty cavern of no great dimensions, but with a lofty, vaulted roof, glowing with a phosphorescent encrustation, which, as Conan knew, was a common phenomenon in that part of the world.</> 
Jewels of Gwahlur

Some shipwrecked Zingaran mercenaries stumbled into Khemi, wild-eyed with a tale of beautiful mermaids who lured half of their company to their death on the shallow reefs off the coast.

Though the sailors were adamant that the naked, beautiful women were fish from the waist down, their reports of "shining smiles" led scholars to suspect that they were native Kushite women chewing a glowing paste that allowed them to prolong their time underwater.

The existence of this paste is well known among the shamans of the Black Kingdoms, though it is rare in the north where the plants that are used in its production do not commonly grow.

<LoreItalics>'Send my soul clean to Asura!'</> - The People of the Black Circle

This tall flower originated in Vendhya, but through trade and happenstance, this hardy bloom can now be found growing in many places the world over. Its magenta hue is much sought after for dyes.

Glass is a fragile substance most often used by nobles and rich merchants for mirrors and windows. Alchemists also prize it for its ability to store volatile concoctions and their ability to observe reactions within the glass as they experiment. Experienced alchemists have hundreds of such flasks, filled with exotic materials from across the world. Less experienced alchemists are probably dead because they stored their concoctions in a less adequate container.
A glass flask filled with water

Alchemists also prize it for its ability to store volatile concoctions and their ability to observe reactions within the glass as they experiment. Experienced alchemists have hundreds of such flasks, filled with exotic materials from across the world. Less experienced alchemists are probably dead because they stored their concoctions in a less adequate container.

This flask is filled with water.
A mold used for creating flasks

Due to their need for somewhere to store volatile concoctions alchemists are usually proficient in the art of glass creation.
It also ensures that if somebody dies due to a flaw in their glasswork releasing a noxious poison into their workshop, they only have themselves to blame.
The heart of a worshipper of Hanuman
This heart was ripped from the chest of a loyal worshipper of Hanuman.

One of the most important facets of the worship of Set is ritual sacrifice. With consecrated blades, the worshippers of Set will cut the hearts from their enemies and offer them as sacrifice on the altar of their demonic god.
For the snakes who gather at the dark altars of the serpent god, human hearts provide a rare delicacy.
Carefully harvested, this meat is ritually pure.

This flesh has not known the touch of a blade and is therefore ritually pure in the eyes of the Yog religion.
The desert men of Darfar, even those who are enslaved in the great city states that make up the kingdom of Shem, partake of ritually pure human flesh at least once every cycle of the moon.
The last lingering presence of the soul

Unlike the other religions of the age, worshippers of Mitra favor dignified and elegant rituals. They frown upon human sacrifice and prefer to perform purification rituals upon the dead.
Ostensibly, this ritual involves positioning the Ankh of Mitra over the body of the deceased and saying a few quiet prayers. The ankh is then touched to the corpse, in order to cleanse it of any last impurities.
Some of the more experienced priests have noticed that at the moment of contant, their ankh becomes slightly heavier, as if something is clinging to the instrument. Those priests are often given vows of silence, shortly thereafter.

This blood, harvested using a ritual tool of Jhebbal Sag, contains something of the ancient past when men and beasts shared a language and hunted by each others side.

This is the essence of Jhebbal Sag, scattered from his divinity and reclaimed, piece by piece, to be offered up in sacrifice at his altars.
Blood purified with the venom of Zath

Taken from a corpse that had been ritually purified by injecting venom, this blood is a the mingled essence of life and the venom of the spider-god Zath.
Such purified blood is useful in the rituals of the spider-god.
A bag woven of spider silk

Woven of the finest strands of spider silk, this bag bears the markings of Zath. Usually carried by a devotee of the religion, it could contain anything from spider eggs to temple valuables. The only way to find out, is to open it.

This note details the rituals and prayers of the Yoggites and contains information about the types of sacrifices and incantations to use to appease the deity. Reading the note will teach you some of gestures and movement to this purpose.

This note contains information about various crafting processes. Reading it will teach you how to properly tinker with things without losing a finger or two.
This note mostly contains a litany of swear-words and crude drawings of gestures. Reading it will teach you a number of taunts.
This note has an aqulionian bedtime story written on it. Reading it will not only teach you the bedtime story but also a variety of sleeping positions.
This note contain extracts from what seems to be an erotic novella called 'Eighty Shades of Pink'. Reading it will teach you how to engage with others before, while, and after bedding them.

This note contain extracts from what seems to be an erotic novella called 'One Hundred Shades of Pink', apparently a sequel to another novella. Reading it will teach you how to engage with others before, while, and after bedding them.

A variety of deep thoughts, such as 'What color is blue - really?' and 'Why can't I lick my own elbow?' are scribbled on this note. Reading it will teach you how to think deeply upon important topics and perhaps you will be the one to finally explain the deep mysteries of the world.
A long list of jokes, seemingly written by a Court Jester. Reading this will teach you these jokes.
Whomever wrote this was truly a spineless coward. Reading this will teach you the same skills. Although why you would want to is a mystery.

The heart of a fallen hero

This heart was taken from the chest of one who once called themselves a hero. The definition shifts between cultures and locations so being sure that one has captured the heart of a hero is a difficult business. Most sorcerers simply content themselves with trying out hundreds of hearts, in the hope that the odds are on their side.
The horn of an ancient rhinoceros
There is a certain energy in the fall of an ancient beast. This horn, taken from an ancient rhinocerous, is an occult focal point. Who knows to what use such an artefact could be put?
This key is of Lemurian origins. It looks like it would fit some of the doors in the Black Keep.
A heart ripped from the chest of the commander of The Silent Legion.
The heart is still beating. The dark energies contained within this heart could be used by a skilled enough craftsman.
A staff topped with a serpentine skull

This staff, found in the acid pit alongside the Abysmal Remnant, is marked with an ancient language. The first runs along the length of the staff in glowing runes, whereas the second is carved rudely over the top of the first script, obscuring pieces of it.

While unintelligible at first glance, beneath the glow of the bracelet, the runes shape themselves into a recognizable script that reads:

"A gift from the ...B... give us advice ...E... and allow us to control the ...T... must be brought ...R... The Tower of the Bat where ...A... placed on the altar ...Y... awakened to share with us ...E... only awakened by ...R... and their blood."

Reading the script is one thing, understanding what it means is something else entirely.
A staff topped with a serpentine skull that has glowing eyes

This staff, awakened during a ritual on top of the Tower of the Bat, seems to be possessed by the spirit of a demon. 

When called upon, the demon can offer advice to the wielder, but whether it can be trusted is a completely different story.
An ornate diadem worn by the Giant-kings

<LoreItalics>Kallian Publico believed that it contained the diadem of the giant-kings, of the people who dwelt in that dark land before the ancestors of the Stygians came there. He showed me a design carved on the lid, which he swore was the shape of the diadem which legend tells us the monster-kings wore.</> - Rogues in the House

Too large to be worn by a human, this diadem hums with contained power. Taken from the Priestking of the Giant-kings - known today as the Barrow King - the story of the diadem is one of betrayal and hatred.

It seems that the Priestking was the father of Tyros the Deathbringer. Tyros turned against his father at some point during the war between the Lemurians and the Giant-kings and his father cursed him, and all of his loyal warriors.

Such is the strength of the diadem, that Tyros and his men were cursed to live forever, a Silent Legion brooding in the ruins of the north.
This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A mask worn by the Witch Queen of Lemuria

<LoreItalics>Many Lemurians escaped to the eastern coast of the Thurian Continent, which was comparatively untouched. There they were enslaved by the ancient race which already dwelt there, and their history, for thousands of years, is a history of brutal servitude.</> - The Hyborian Age

This mask was used by the Witch Queens of Lemuria to communicate with their primary deity, Dagon, before their kingdom sank into the ocean during the cataclysm.

When the Lemurians crossed into the land of the Giant-kings, they negotiated for somewhere to settle. The Witch Queen, weary of the forced exile of her people, helped the Giant-kings to forge the bracelets, originally to facilitate communication between the two races.

Later, this mask possessed the exile Razma, controlling her thoughts and forcing her to start rebuilding the palace at the heart of Xel-ha.
This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A crystalline tear from Tyros the Deathbringer

<LoreItalics>Tears rolled from the sightless eyes, and Conan's gaze strayed to the limbs stretched on the marble couch. And he knew the monster would not rise to attack him. He knew the marks of the rack, and the searing brand of the flame, and tough-souled as he was, he stood aghast at the ruined deformities which his reason told him had once been limbs as comely as his own. And suddenly all fear and repulsion went from him to be replaced by a great pity.</> - The Tower of the Elephant

This single tear, shed by Tyros the Deathbringer, is an object of immense power. Tyros, was the half-blood child of  the Priestking and an unknown human slave. Whether his birth was natural or aided by sorcery, is not known, but it is known that Tyros had children of his own with his wife, Telith.

Tyros was raised a gladiator, fighting in the arena for the benefit of the Giant-kings, but when war broke out with the Lemurians, he became a leader in their armies. Through great feats of strength and will, he won the outpost of Xullan from the Lemurian army. Just south of there, he met Telith, a daughter of Lemuria, and everything changed...

This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A crazy angled stone kept within an alien box

<LoreItalics>It was treasured and placed in its curious box by the crinoid things of Antarctica, salvaged from their ruins by the serpent-men of Valusia... "</> - The Haunter of the Dark, H.P. Lovecraft

This artefact is spoken of in whispers by the nighted cults of the Hyborian age. It is rumored to be a window into all of space and time - but with the cost that the user risks baring their soul to powers from the outer dark.

The Serpentmen of Valusia were in possession of this object, and how they came to be living beneath the volcano in the Exiled Lands is a mystery. Perhaps fleeing their genocide at the hands of the legendary Kull of Atlantis, they made their way to the Exiled Lands where they befriended the Giant-kings through worship of their deity, Set. In return they were allowed to live in the Caldera of the volcano and build their cities there.

It was, however, too late for the serpent men, a degenerate and dying race, lacking the genetic diversity to continue. They found themselves coupling with snakes and lesser reptiles in the hope of preserving their species but as time passed, they lost all hope of survival and instead, preyed for bitter revenge upon the races.

They crafted a staff with their ancient magics and summoned a presence via the trapezohedron, to inhabit the staff and lead the Giant-kings to their downfall.

If they must die, they would take as many with them as possible and most especially, the cursed children of humankind.

This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A gleaming jewel on an ornate pin

<LoreItalics>So you could steal from him the only thing he would never give you -- the ring with the jewel men call the Star of Khorala -- the star stolen from the queen of Ophir, who would pay a roomful of gold for its return. He would not give it to you willingly, because he knew that it holds a magic which, when properly controlled, will enslave the hearts of any of the opposite sex.</> - Shadows in Zamboula

The Star of the Champion is a gem of unsurpassed beauty - glowing with a white light that sets the world to shimmering. 

Once, in the ancient past, it was awarded to Tyros the Deathbringer for becoming the champion of the Giant-kings arena. 

In his final battle, he was to fight the mightiest dragon created by the Giant-kings, a magnificent creature of enormous stature. Tyros defeated the beast, but in his victory, he saw the death of something noble and he wept. He pinned the Star of the Champion to the corpse of the creature - and the mighty beast was buried right there, beneath the sands of the arena.

Later, when Tyros was cursed with immortality, the dragon inherited the curse and rose again to stalk the arena.

This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A stone containing an enslaved elemental

<LoreItalics>He it was who shook down the cliffs at Valkia, by his spells that enthrall the elementals of the earth-he it was who sent the creature of darkness into your tent before dawn.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Also known as the Scourgestone, this unassuming chunk of stone contains the elemental that plagues the Exiled Lands with continual sandstorms.

Enslaved by the Priestking in his desperation to end the war after the Shattering on the Plains, he gave it over to the Warmaker to release at the right moment.

When the time came, the Warmaker shattered the stone into fragments and scattered them across the battlefield, freeing the elemental to do its work.

It seemed to work, gathering a gigantic storm that crossed the Exiled Lands, moving towards the city of Xel-ha in the far east.
But the Giant-kings had not reckoned with the power of the human spirit. A Lemurian priest named Petruso went out to confront the sandstorm. Using the power of Dagon, he anchored the elemental controlling the sandstorm to his flesh, preventing it from moving further east and destroying the Lemurian city.

He saved his people, yes, but Petruso paid a terrible price. His sacrifice had not stopped the sandstorm, it had simply put it into a temporal loop. It passed across the Exiled Lands, time and time again, stopping when it reached Petruso... then starting again.

Eventually this drove him insane.

This is one of the artefacts required to create the keystone that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A black essence left by the Servant of the Ring

<LoreItalics>By Set, mine enemy knew not the hour when he might awake at midnight to feel the taloned fingers of a nameless horror at his throat! I did dark and terrible magic with the Serpent Ring of Set, which I found in a nighted tomb a league beneath the earth, forgotten before the first man crawled out of the slimy sea.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

Thoth Amon of the Black Ring is the man who created the Exiled Lands.

During one of his journeys seeking sorcerous knowledge, he stumbled upon the Unnamed City and, befriending the lone survivor, Warmaker Klael, he soon learned of the powerful artefacts contained beneath the city.

Exploring the ruins, he found the Serpent Ring of Set, and the slave bracelets of the Giant-kings. In his twisted mind, a plan began to form.
A deal was struck with King Cstephon of Stygia. Thoth Amon would provide the bracelets and a place where the political and ideological enemies of the king could be exiled forever (but kept alive as a contingency for the future) and in return, King Cstephon would provide troops to occasionally ride through the Exiled Lands and collect any artefacts that the poor unfortunates had obtained.

This then was the founding of the Exiled Lands and the Purge, though over the years the deal has altered and Thoth Amon has extended his offer to other rulers across the world (without the knowledge of King Cstephon, naturally).

Thoth Amon has moved further and further from the concerns of the  worldly - he no longer deals personally with the affairs of the Exiled Lands. Instead, he sends his enforcer, the Servant of the Ring to deal with any major problems.

This essence, taken from the Servant of the Ring, hopefully contains enough of the dark sorcery to complete the ritual to create the keystone, that can be used to remove the slave bracelet.
A jagged piece of stone that pulses with power
This is a piece of the legendary Scourgestone. But it is broken and must be reassembled by one who understands the power that it holds.
A shattered piece of stone that pulses with power
This is a piece of the legendary Scourgestone. But it is broken and must be reassembled by one who understands the power that it holds.
A broken piece of stone that pulses with power
This is a piece of the legendary Scourgestone. But it is broken and must be reassembled by one who understands the power that it holds.
A keystone that unlocks the bracelet

This keystone, created through a ritual, contains the essence of the artefacts that were used to create the slave bracelets of the Giant-kings.

It can be used to remove a slave bracelet from one who is exiled. This is an extremely powerful artefact and must be used with caution.
Simply use the item to remove the bracelet.

WARNING: REMOVING THE BRACELET WILL END THE GAME AND DELETE YOUR CHARACTER!
A key to open the door to Razma's Quarters
This small key opens a door in Sepermeru,  which is where Razma returned after being freed from the Mask of the Witch Queen.
A mixture for hardening stone pieces

The Exiled Lands stand as a testament to the efficacy of weather at destroying the works of man. When the wind howls across the landscape and the sand scours everything in its path, there are few buildings that survive for very long.
However, the supernaturally large insects of the Exiled Lands have developed a natural secretion that helps to protect them against the environment. 
Ichor from these creatures, when soaked into twine and bound to a stone surface, can be placed into a furnace and hardened into bricks that provide excellent protection against the rigors of the Exiled Lands.
An iron frame used to reinforce walls.
The weakness of stone lies in the spaces between the bricks themselves and the materials that bind them together. This reinforcement, crafted of iron, helps to create a solid frame for the stones.
A steel frame used to reinforce walls.
The weakness of stone lies in the spaces between the bricks themselves and the materials that bind them together. This reinforcement, crafted of steel, helps to create a solid frame for the stones.

Loose fitting stones are a poor defense against the elements and the creatures of the Exiled Lands. Bricks, cut from sections of sandstone, provide more strength to structures and can be butressed with iron and steel to create sturdy walls and strong defenses.

These bricks are shaped to fit, but have not undergone any more specific treatment.

The term is used for too wide an array of strong drinks, of various qualities, often made from whatever is on hand. With any luck, the drinker will spend the night drunk and not wake up blind. It certainly heats the tongue.

<LoreItalics>You laugh greatly, drink deep and bellow good songs; though I never saw another Cimmerian who drank aught but water, or who ever laughed, or ever sang save to chant dismal dirges.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

Many lands and many people claim the discovery of mead, to be the first to learn that the already wondrous foodstuff of the bee could be fermented into something yet more wondrous. The Aesir and Vanir of Nordheim often seal pacts made in Ymir's name with three successive drinks of mead. A sip of this honeyed brew warms the tongue.
A dark wine with a burning bouquet

<LoreItalics>Ascalante turned again to his wine. Over the jeweled spires was rising a dawn crimson as blood.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

This wine is made using resin, darkening its color. It leaves the drinker feeling warmed.
Bounty of the grape, drink of the gods

<LoreItalics>Let me live deep while I live; let me know the rich juices of red meat and stinging wine on my palate, the hot embrace of white arms, the mad exultation of battle when the blue blades flame and crimson, and I am content.</> - Queen of the Black Coast

The alcoholic beverage made from the grape. Different grapes and different techniques in their fermentation produce different vintages. Wine lightly cools the tongue.

<LoreItalics>In front of him stood Tsotha, and on divans lounged Strabonus and Amalrus in their silks and gold, gleaming with jewels, naked slave-boys beside them pouring wine into cups carved of a single sapphire.</> - The Scarlet Citadel

A technique out of Arogs uses honey in the processes of fermenting the pulped grapes, producing a wine that is both sweet and medicinal. This is indeed a drink that blesses one's health.

<LoreItalics>'Wine!' gasped the king from the couch where they had laid him. They put a goblet to his bloody lips and he drank like a man half dead of thirst.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

A light-colored wine, popular in Turan, known to ease a throat that has taken in the dust of the desert roads. It cools the tongue more than the average vintage.
Smells kind of funny, but tastes ok

<LoreItalics>The dullest was struck by the contrast between the harsh, taciturn, gloomy commander, and the pirate whose laugh was gusty and ready, who roared ribald songs in a dozen languages, guzzled ale like a toper, and - apparently - had no thought for the morrow.</> - The Pool of the Black One

There are those who like to put a little something extra in their drink. This beer adds particular strains of mushrooms to the brewing process. Some claim they receive visions in the night after such a draught, but these may just be the dreams of the drunk. This beer heats the tongue.
A bizarre gland that can be used to make explosives

Harvested from the corpse of a degenerate, imp-like creature found in the Exiled Lands, this gland is a key component for making demon-fire orbs.
The mechanism by which these creatures cause themselves to explode is not well understood, though scholars in other lands have reported similar incidents with frogs and ants. 
Most, however, simple agree that the explosions are sorcerous in nature and leave it at that.
Both the savage and the civilized mouth water when strips of meat sizzle and hiss on the skewer.

<LoreItalics>It takes an Argossean merchant to wring wealth out of a little waterfront shop that stank of rotten fish and cheap wine.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

The bounty of the rivers and seas are a major food source for many peoples in Hyboria. Such fare may be prepared by roasting, boiling, and many other methods besides.

An assortment of shellfish, hot and prepared
Shellfish comprise a large category of varied and tasty fare. Such meaty bounty can be plucked right from the waters, but cooking reduces the risk of sickness.

<LoreItalics>She gave into his hands a wooden dish heaped with dried  fruits, cheese and barley bread, and a great pot of the heady upland beer, brewed from barley grown in the high valleys.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Bread takes on many forms, baked from various mixtures of dough and water. On the climb from savagery, bread tends to come at the dawn of agriculture.
A decadent display of choice meats

<LoreItalics>His life was a series of feasts and wild debauches. He filled his palace with the fairest girls of the kingdom, willing or unwilling. He blasphemed the gods and sprawled drunken on the floor of the banquet hall wearing the golden crown, and staining his royal purple robes with the wine he spilled.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Some eat merely to survive another savage day. Others, of a sensual bent, create magnificent feasts of the most exotic meats, feasts that would make the gods salivate unto a deluge. Decadence to the point of madness? Perhaps. But there is something to be said for the great boon of health this grants the eater.
Heaps and heaps of glorious meat

<LoreItalics>Wolves prowled openly along the grass-grown highways, and bands of gaunt, masterless men slunk through the forests. Only in Tarantia was feasting and wealth and pageantry.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Large game, in quantity, make for a meal that would put an army of bellies glad. Such a meal offers good health to the eater.
A tasty combination of food from the land and the sea.
Dark green egg smelling of ammonia

There is a method of preserving eggs, developed in faraway Khitai. The details vary among the people, but this method often involves clay or ash or salt or quicklime. The egg, so preserved, turns to a dark green. Those foreign to the practice often only eat such an egg out of desperation or a drunken dare. There is the chance that the one who preserved it did not use the ancient method precisely. An imperfectly preserved egg might bring terrible sickness to the eater.

Water is necessary for life, yet it is not always pure. One can risk sickness by drinking from a strange water source. Humankind has learned different methods of purifying their water, from charcoal to boiling.
A ritualistic meal in honor of Yog

<LoreItalics>There were grisly feasts beneath the moon, across whose red disk a bat-like shadow incessantly swept.</> - Queen of the Black Coast

This feast is consumed in the name of Yog. Yog, the Lorde of Empty Abodes! Yog, cousin of them that slither in the immaculate slime of the Elder Night! All good and fearing worshipers of Yog must dedicate themselves to the consumption of only meat. All the faithful of Yog must taste human flesh once a month, lest they become unclean until they again perform this communion of body and blood.
A feast of various gamey meats. What such a meal lacks in quality, it makes up for quantity. Gorging on such fare can satisfy the belly and offer a little relief to the injured.
Strips of feral meat dried and salted
Meat can be preserved for a time by salting and drying. The process also improves the flavor, or perhaps covers it up, of stringy and gamy meat.
A foreboding liquid of acrid yet sweet aroma

<LoreItalics>Even the arts you call sorcery are governed by cosmic laws.</> - The People of the Black Circle

Foul ingredients are brewed together to make this forbidden drink which corrupts body and soul. Sorcerers covet this libation, for they know that it nourishes a certain, long atrophied organ of the human soul, stimulating it to open like a nocturnal flower and become sensitive to the vibrations and blasphemies of the Outer Dark.
Gruel with a dash of flavor
Spices, ingredients, and oddities often get thrown into gruel to mask the fact that all one has to eat is gruel.
A zesty haunch of exotic meat

There are clubs and cliques among the elite nobles of Zingara that pride themselves on devouring exotic fare. The rarest of meals. There are rumors such organizations employ warlocks simply to summon otherworldly horrors, just so the dinner guests may dine on its spectral flesh. Whatever the truth, they do enjoy spicing their meats until they pleasantly heat the pallet.
A ritualistic meal in honor of Set

<LoreItalics>Their ghastly feasts were considered a sacrifice to the scaly god.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

This feast is consumed in the name of Set. Set, the Old Serpent! Set. Archenemy Iblis! Set, who is known as Damballah in the Southern kingdoms, whose holy scales blind all with their bright darkness! Set is a jealous god and requires constant sacrifices from his chosen. This meal is devoured as an offering to the Lord of Snakes. May it grow a nest of serpents in the belly of the eater.
Any Zingaran buccaneer will swear to a very specific regimen before a night of passionate romance:  to devour a dozen spiced oysters in quick succession. This seafood heats the pallet.
The fruit of the shell, the bounty of the sea, cooked and safe for consumption. Oysters have a way of becoming a delicacy to most any culture that rests on the water's edge.
This drink, made from squeezed berries, is sweet to the taste and lightly cools the parched tongue.
A ritualistic meal in honor of Mitra

<LoreItalics>Mitra grant that I do not fail of this mighty trust!</> - The Hour of the Dragon

This feast is consumed in the name of Mitra. Mitra, chief god of Hyboria! Mitra, the righteous, the father of justice, the enemy of Set! May this meal open a holy and eternal spring in the belly.  May man's heart know mercy. Mitra, guard us against the powers of darkness.
Waste not, want not. When a variety of meat scraps accrue, it is prudent to gather them and cook them all together before they spoil.
A hearty bowl of broth and other bits of food
When one has a fresh bone and water and a few other odds and ends left over, they have enough to make a satisfying soup.
It is gruel, but it actually smells good
Sometimes one is able to find a few extra things to throw into the gruel, to make it a more satisfying meal.

<LoreItalics>It is not against men I must shield you. There are dark worlds barely guessed by man, wherein formless monsters stalk - fiends which may be drawn from the Outer Voids to take material shape and rend and devour at the bidding of evil magicians.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

It is said that the long-dead sage Epemitreus devised a modest brew, by steeping a very particular mix of herbs and ingredients in boiling water, that could cleanse a small amount of the corrupting influence of the Outer Dark from one's mind and body.

Strong tea, steeped with potent spices, can drastically refresh one's stamina while heating the body and mind. Turanian guards who draw the late shift are said to be quite fond of this drink on cold, desert nights.

<LoreItalics>He was a magician from far Khitai, returning to his native kingdom after a journey to Stygia. He took me with him to purple-towered Paikang, its minarets rising amid the vine-festooned jungles of bamboo, and there I grew to womanhood under his teaching.</> - A Witch Shall Be Born

This brew, a recipe from far away Khitai, revitalizes one's stamina in small measures.
Strips of exotic meat dried and salted

There are those who say drying and salting such fare is a waste of superior meat, but there are also those who want a finer sort of dry ration to reach into their bag for on faraway and lonely trails.
Slice of meat and sizzling eggs
When one can spare a cut of succulent meat, a breakfast of eggs becomes a heartier meal that makes the heart happy and the belly more than full.

There are those who like the natural taste of the meat, cooked rare so that one's teeth still draw blood. And there are those who prefer to inundate their meat with all manner of spices. This dish heats the pallet.
Strips of succulent meat dried and salted
Many a hungry soul, when seeing a fine cut of meat from large game, desire to devour it all in one sitting. The wiser sort know when to ration off a bit and salt and dry it for hungrier nights ahead.
Both the savage and the civilized mouth water when strips of meat sizzle and hiss on the skewer.
Full of things with no legs or too many legs

The tribes of Darfar know how to find hidden sustenance. Certain grubs and meaty insects, combined with certain herbs, make for a surprisingly refreshing soup. Served cold, this dish moderately cools the pallet.
Zingarans are known for making a spicy soup that puts a little fire in one's belly, heating the pallet.
A green soup with no meat at all

Many a survivor knows to apply the juice of the aloe to a burn or to seek the plant's moisture when trekking out in the hot wastes, but certain crones and culinary masters know the healing properties of cooking aloe in a soup. Such a meal offers seemingly instant and moderate relief to the injured.
The bounty of plants are many, and a surplus of seeds can be turned into a filling soup.
Soup boiled from that infamous blossom

<LoreItalics>He halted at an ebony door, in the center of which was a grinning silver skull, and pushed it open. He looked into a chamber of ebony and jet, and saw, on a black silken couch, a tall, spare form reclining. Yara the priest and sorcerer lay before him, his eyes open and dilated with the fumes of the yellow lotus, far-staring, as if fixed on gulfs and nighted abysses beyond human ken.</> - The Tower of the Elephant

While the yellow lotus can make a mind forget its past, one may cook it into a soup and boil out this property. So prepared, it becomes a safe and rather mundane meal, despite the mystical mystique surrounding the flower.
A surplus of mushrooms can make a surprisingly hearty stew.
Some mushrooms are poisonous, it is true, but many can be cooked into a culinary delight. Properly prepared, roasted mushrooms are good for the eater's health over time.
Hot and smelling of winter spices
This special brew, heated and loaded with mulled spices, heavily warms a soul even on the longest of winter nights.

<LoreItalics>'They have no hope here or hereafter,' answered Conan. 'Their gods are Crom and his dark race, who rule over a sunless place of everlasting mist, which is the world of the dead. Mitra! The ways of the Aesir were more to my liking.'</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

The Cimmerians are a hearty people, and they make their meals equally hearty when they can afford to. But Cimmerians are also a grim people, and things such as spice and flavor rarely touch their tongues.
Shroom tea with a zesty kick

<LoreItalics>The full lips opened and spoke a single word, in a rich vibrant tone that was like the golden chimes that ring in the jungle-lost temples of Khitai.</> - The God in the Bowl

The mystics of jungle-cradled Khitai know of certain fungi to brew in their tea, for the purposes of expanding their consciousness to fathom realms both resplendently bright and dark as the nighted voids.
Chunks of succulent meat floating in a stew
Meat chopped up and cooked in a broth of vegetables makes for a simmering stew that smells both inviting and filling.

The blood and flesh of demons are not only components to the profane rituals of sorcerers... but also the culinary arts of the adventurous. These links of cooked meat seem to pulse with eldritch life and eating such fare bestows strong recuperative powers, over time, to the eater.
Soup from a great beast's head

There is a very specialized school of divination magic that suggests the future can be divined in a broiled rhinoceros head. There are also hunters who swear the powder of a rhino horn will imbue a man with virility. The veracity of these claims is highly suspect. What is known is that a soup, boiled from the head of a rhino, will imbue the eater with greater power to carry a heavy load.
A meal heavy with fat will stay in one's stomach, and keep them well fed for some time.
Zesty meat wrapped in crocodile skin

It is said that pirates from the Black Coast created this delicacy by wrapping strips of meat in crocodile skin, heavily spicing the concoction, and then cooking it all until it is crackling crisp. This dish heats one's pallet.
Chunks of exotic meat floating in a fine stew
Only the choicest cuts of meat go into this superior stew.
A specialty of desert caravans. Whatever meat is available is mixed and stewed and livened with copious amounts of spice. This dish will heavily heat the pallet.
A meal both filling and flavorful
Only the heartiest meals can prepare one for the savage world.
Under the delicious broth is something that was recently...human

<LoreItalics>Yet what creature but man breaks bones for their marrow? Perhaps those remnants were mute evidence of a horrible, cannibalistic feast...</> - The Hour of the Dragon

A delicacy out of Darfar. The proper way to serve this delicious, hot broth is with a hull human skull in the bowl, slowly revealed with every slurping spoonful.

One of the best uses for strong spice is to improve the flavor of gamey meat, shredded to make up for this chewy toughness. Tavern owners share a proverb: 'A dead rat and a jar of spice will get you a lot further in life than just a dead rat.' This dish heats the pallet.

A trick learned from the people of Kush is to skewer assortments of large insects and grubs, with bits of vegetable or fruit for flavor, and roast it all on a fire. It makes for a surprisingly tasty treat.
Eggs can be livened up with the right spices. This dish warms the pallet.

<LoreItalics>From the deep gash flowed a strange ichor, and Khosatral cried out like the dirging of a great bell.</> - The Devil in Iron

These innocent-looking eggs hide a gleeful treachery. Within the obfuscation of the shell there resides a blasphemous gush of ichor. Some sadistic nobles relish springing such a surprise on their guests, savoring the looks on their masticating faces.
Eggs make for a fine, storable food, given by nature in their own containers. Cracked open, eggs cook quickly.
These berries have been dried to preserve them. They do not offer much nourishment, but will resist decay for a time.
A small snack both savory and sweet
A common food practice in Turan is to mix salt with certain sweet fruits. This snack, of salted berries, is both tasty and a little better preserved.
A ritualistic meal in honor of Ymir

<LoreItalics>Tall and fair and blue-eyed. Their god is Ymir, the frost-giant, and each tribe has its own king. They are wayward and fierce. They fight all day and drink ale and roar their wild songs all night.</> - The Phoenix on the Sword

This feast is consumed in the name of Ymir. Ymir, the Frost Giant and father of all lesser giants! Ymir, Lord of Storm and War! May he grant the strength to fight all of the day and drink all of the night. May this meal grant a warrior the bravery to die in battle, earning a place in Ymir's hall in Valhalla to feast and revel until the end of days.
Raw flesh harvested from an oyster
This flesh is harvested from an oyster. It is known as a delicacy in many places, and rumored to increase virility.
A small turtle, full of delicious potential
A small turtle heavy with fat that will stay in one's stomach and keep them well fed for some time. Quite cute as well.

<LoreItalics>Nay, my men are sick to stretch their legs ashore, and nigh to scurvy from chewing salt pork.</> - The Black Stranger

Civilization pivots around salt, communities forming, like growths, around sources of the stuff. Salt is mined, and it is boiled from salt-laden water. It flavors food. Sometimes, it serves as a form of currency. Perhaps most importantly, salt is the best known food preserver, especially for meat.

<LoreItalics>Some vagrant scent of spice or palm woke clear-etched images of strange coasts where mangroves grew and drums thundered, of ships locked in battle and decks running blood, of smoke and flame and the crying of slaughter...</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Taken from the seeds, fruit, roots, and bark of plants, spices are used in cooking, medicine, and the arcane arts. These potent flavors hailed from the east, from Turan, Vendhya, and far away Khitai. The insatiable desire of Stygians to procure spices for their mummification rituals expanded trade along the continent. Flavoring one's food with spice warms the soul for a time.

This brew, a recipe from far away Khitai, revitalizes one's stamina in small measures, and moderately heals the wary and injured over time.
Bigger is always better no matter what they say
Some tinctures are useful. Others are merely... engorging.
Links of meat held together by innards. Tasty.
Loved by some, hated by most - blood sausages are a staple food amongst the tribes of the frozen north. Every part of the animal is used, even the blood that courses through their veins.
A meal heavy with fat will stay in one's stomach, and keep them well fed for some time.
A meal heavy with fat will stay in one's stomach, and keep them well fed for some time.
Raw flesh harvested from a wild boar

Raw meat is a dangerous temptation for the starving and desperate. Consuming it provides immediate relief from hunger - but at the risk of inheriting any disease or parasite that may have come along for the ride.
Only the heartiest meals can prepare one for the savage world.

A cooked haunch of exquisite meat
A cooked haunch of the best meat these lands have to offer.

A salted piece of meat with perfect texture
Salted to perfection, this meat will last.
A spiced piece of meat with perfect texture
