<LoreItalics>The giants answered with roars like the grinding of icebergs on a frozen shore and heaved up their shining axes as the maddened Cimmerian hurled himself upon them.</> - The Frost Giant's Daughter

This axe is rimed in frost and decorated with the angular runes of the Nordheimers. The haft thrums with power and the presence of Ymir emanates from the weapon itself.

This is a sacred weapon, imbued with the blessing of a deity. Use it well.
A powerful sword blessed by Derketo

<LoreItalics>I am a daughter of Luxur, and before I had known fifteen summers I had been led through the temples of Derketo, the dusky goddess, and had been initiated into the mysteries.</> - Xuthal of the Dusk

This sword, suggestively shaped, seems to twist and bend as light plays across the blade. There is a dark ritual, performed naked by the priests and priestesses of Derketa, that involves this blade, a sacrificial victim and necrophilia. 

Derketo it is said, appears in person to lick the blood from the blade.

This is a sacred weapon, imbued with the blessing of a deity.
A powerful two-handed staff blessed by Mitra

<LoreItalics> But the voice called him on, and at last, in darkness that would have been impenetrable to his material eyes, he came into a strange crypt, and saw a vague white-bearded figure sitting on a tomb.</>  - The Phoenix on the Sword

When the world was young, there was a great sage known as Epemitreus. Little is known of the shadowy past in which he fought with Set, the arch-demon, but it is known that for all the days of his life he strove against the worshippers, votaries and acolytes of the Old Serpent.

It is rumored that in times of need the ghost of Epemitreus flies on unseen wings to aid the kingdom of Aquilonia, and that the symbol of the phoenix belongs to the sage as much as it does to Mitra.

This staff is crafted from a pattern created by the sage Epemitreus. It is marked with a simple script which reads: 'By fire and steel and the juice of the Upas tree'

This is a sacred weapon, imbued with the blessing of a deity.
A powerful mace blessed by Yog

The rough appearance of this mace belies the terrible power concealed within. Decorated with the swirling symbols that make up a single syllable of the unutterable name of Yog, this mace is heavy with the darkness of Yog.

This is a sacred weapon, imbued with the blessing of a deity.
A powerful set of daggers blessed by Set

Rumored to be fangs that were shed by the great serpent himself, this matched set of carved daggers have been passed by archpriest to archpriest for centuries. They are stained to the hilt in the blood of sacrifice - glorious sacrifice in the name of Set.
These are sacred weapons, imbued with the blessing of a deity.
Claws that unleash the rage of the beast

<LoreItalics>A man from the Tauran couldn't mistake the mark of a panther's claws. No. It's a forest devil summoned by Zogar Sag to carry out his revenge.</> - Beyond the Black River

With these equipped, the world takes on a red tinge. The power of Jhebbal Sag surges and the beast takes control.

With these equipped, new combinations of moves unlock and a warrior becomes a feral beast in combat.
Heavy, unwieldy hammer for repairing structures

<LoreItalics>Khosatral Khel rose and lived and waxed mighty once more. It pleased him to restore the city as it was in the days before its fall.</> - The Devil in Iron

Crafted for utility, this hammer is an unwieldy tool when used for anything other than pounding on stone or wood.

It is inevitable that time, the elements, and the beasts of the Exiled Lands will take their toll on structures. With the repair hammer and the correct combination of materials, almost anything can be repaired with a few hefty swings.

Like cultures and customs, the value of ivory depends upon the kingdom where it is seen.

In the Hyborian kingdoms, where elephants and other creatures are rare, it is a tangible sign of both wealth and power. In the Black Kingdoms, it is common - few warriors exist in those lands who do not possess an ivory handled dagger or jewelry.

It is a great source of trade between the north and the south - indeed it could be said that ivory is the primary reason that merchants dare make the dangerous journey along the Black Coast to trade for it in Kush.

This ivory arrow, honed to perfection, is excellently balanced and will cause great damage.

A massive hammer of black glass

A sharp-edged, glassy stone. Not easily worked like iron or steel, obsidian can still be made into ridiculously brittle weapons.

Mauls and warhammers are slow to swing and leave their user vulnerable to counterattack, but when they connect they are brutally effective. Armored foes are particularly vulnerable to these massive blunt weapons which break bones, shatter skulls and crush spines.
A two-handed sword of black glass

<LoreItalics>'I pay my way with steel!' roared the man in armor, brandishing the great sword that glittered bluely in the sun. 'By Crom, man, if you don't get under way, I'll drench this galley in the blood of its crew!'</> - Queen of the Black Coast

Forged in the depths of the Volcano that looms over the Exiled Lands, this sword is made of obsidian. It is brittle, but the sharp facets of the black glass will cause additional damage to opponents.

Great swords are faster than many other two-handed weapons, and their great reach makes them ideal for fending off groups of opponents.
Short, sharp blades of black glass

Forged in the depths of the Volcano that looms over the Exiled Lands, these daggers are made of obsidian. They are brittle, but the sharp facets of the black glass will cause additional damage to opponents.

Daggers are a weapon used with passion by the untrained and with a cold dispassion by the trained. Unseasoned warriors consider swords the superior weapon - until they come across a master, twin blades flashing as they dash and dart within the reach of their enemies and disembowel them.

<LoreItalics>The three soldiers-men-at-arms wearing the emblem of the royal guards-rushed at the king, and one felled the squire with a blow of a mace.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Forged in the depths of the Volcano that looms over the Exiled Lands, this mace is made of obsidian. It is brittle, but the sharp facets of the black glass will cause additional damage to opponents.

Capable of shattering bones through armor and crumpling helmets, the mace is a preferred weapon against heavily armored foes, bypassing the protection of their armor through sheer force.

<LoreItalics>The Stygians had discarded their bows; helmeted heads bent to the blast, dark eyes glaring over the rims of their shields, they came on in an inexorable surge, striding over their fallen comrades.</> - Black Colossus

Forged in the depths of the Volcano that looms over the Exiled Lands, this shield is made of obsidian. Nobody knows what the purpose of a glass shield is, but perhaps the black glass is strengthened when formed into such a lattice.

Most warriors prefer to carry a shield into battle if there is one available. The best blow is the one that misses, but the second-best blow is the one that you block.

With superior reach the pike is a common weapon on the battlefields of Hyboria. The most effective use of the pike is from behind the lines of battle, thrusting into the gaps in a shield wall.

The thick haft and weighted end mean that the pike must be wielded in two hands.

Forged in the depths of the Volcano that looms over the Exiled Lands, this sword is made of obsidian. It is brittle, but the sharp facets of the black glass will cause additional damage to opponents.

Swords are straight-bladed, one-handed weapons, both fast and reliable.

<LoreItalics>And at last mankind conquered, so long ago that naught but dim legends come to us through the ages. The snake-people were the last to go, yet at last men conquered even them and drove them forth into the waste lands of the world, there to mate with true snakes until some day, say the sages, the horrid breed shall vanish utterly.</> - The Shadow Kingdom

The snake-people were thought to be gone. First defeated in the war with first man at the dawn of time, then purged again by King Kull of Valusia.

But here, in this bizarre, mysterious piece of the world, they found succor with the Giant-kings. Perhaps the city in the volcano was ancient before even the Giant-kings lived in this land. But either way, the degenerate remnant remains.

Legendary tulwar of a Wazuli Chief

<LoreItalics>Conan lifted his knife and smote, and the watchers were dumbfounded to see his blow checked apparently in midair, with the loud clang of steel that meets an unyielding substance. He wasted no more effort. He knew that not even the legendary tulwar of Amir Khurum could shatter that invisible curtain.</> - The People of the Black Circle

Amir Khurum was a legendary prince and commander of the Wazuli tribe. The Wazuli revere his memory for his even-handed nature as a chief - he dealt honorably with all and led them to a great deal of treasure in his career.

The origins of this blade are mysteriously absent from any record. Those who have possessed it over the years claim that it fills them with a nameless hunger for blood.

Once the sword was taken to oracle who named it a dark spirit that crosses between worlds and time endlessly, in search of shattered men in shattered lands who will let it drink.

This sword seems to drain additional life from the enemy with every hit, soaking it into the very surface of the sword.
A blade that glimmers with unholy life

The scars of the war that tore the Exiled Lands apart thousands of years in the past are still apparent today. And the dead walk the ancient battlefields, carrying weapons that glimmer with ancient sorrow.

This blade, taken from one of the dead, allows the vitality of the dead to seep into the bearer. Its unearthly light reminds the wielder that death is the consequence of living, and thus encourages them to live just a little more strongly.

This weapon increases vitality.
A long, pointed blade suited for dueling

<LoreItalics>Framed in his steel morion his face was dark, saturnine and hawk-like, wherefore men called him the Hawk. His armor and garments were rich and ornate, after the fashion of a Zingaran grandee. His hand was never far from his sword-hilt.</> - Pool of the Black One

Zaporavo, known as the Hawk, was a nobleman in Zingara known for his dueling prowess, defeating all of the champions of Kordava to become a premiere swordsman in the kingdom.

However, due to his pride, Zaporavo was unable to allow himself to lose. During a bout with the King of Zingara, where tradition demands that the king be allowed to win, Zaporavo drew first blood. 

The king was furious and Zaporavo was exiled. He cast his dueling blade from the docks of Kordava, and then left the city forever, becoming the Captain of the Wastrel and a terror to those who sailed the Zingaran coastline.

<LoreItalics>Shifting his reddened scimitar to his left hand, he drew the great half-blade of the Yuetshi. Khosatral Khel was towering above him, his arms lifted like mauls, but as the blade caught the sheen of the sun, the giant gave back suddenly.</> - The Devil in Iron

Forged of a meteor, which flashed through the sky like a flaming arrow, this long, crescent blade is of another world. 
It was used to cut down and enthrall Khosatral Khel, an unearthly being of untold power, before it suddenly disappeared - and reappeared here, in the Exiled Lands.

When used, it gives unearthly strength in battle.
A set of matched poniards bearing the inscription Grim

<LoreItalics>He inspected the weapon the girl had given him and smiled grimly. Whatever else she might be, she was proven by that dagger to be a person of practical intelligence. It was no slender stiletto, selected because of a jeweled hilt or gold guard, fitted only for dainty murder in milady's boudoir; it was a forthright poniard, a warrior's weapon, broad-bladed, fifteen inches in length, tapering to a diamond-sharp point.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

About twenty years ago, a murderer stalked the streets of Belverus, the capital of Nemedia. Every night, young men and women would go missing from the streets, and their corpses would be found later, mutilated and laid at the doorsteps of their homes.

The people cried out for the murderer to be captured and the watchmen found a suspect, a middle-aged lamplighter who was captured with two blood-stained poniards during his rounds one night.

For his part, the lamplighter told an unbelievable story. He claimed to have seen the poniards floating through the air of their own accord. He said that when he moved towards them, they turned and flew at his throat. Ducking aside, he turned to find that they had embedded themselves in the sideboard of his cart. 

Despite this wild story, he was hanged for his crimes. The murders ceased. And the city slept. And the poniards were never seen again.

These poniards, when used in battle, will increase the damage of every strike.
A pair of peshkabz stained with blood

<LoreItalics>Sobbing wildly, Yasmina plucked a jeweled dagger from her girdle and plunged it to the hilt in his breast. He stiffened and then went limp, a grim smile curving his dead lips. Yasmina hurled herself face-down on the rush-covered floor, beating the reeds with her clenched hands. Outside, the gongs and conchs brayed and thundered, and the priests gashed themselves with copper knives.</> - The People of the Black Circle

The peshkabz of Vendhya are designed to pierce armor, passing through layers of steel to strike at the flesh beneath.
This matched pair is whispered to have been used to murder kings, and that the stain on the blade from the royal blood can never be removed.

<LoreItalics>Thrusting his dagger-point into the crack, Conan exerted leverage with a corded forearm. The blade bent, but it was of unbreakable Akbitanan steel.</> - Jewels of Gwahlur

The expertise of the smiths of Akbitana combined with a local source of ore that has special qualities, provides the hardest steel weapon on earth.

Usually only sold in the city itself, these daggers are a very rare find. They will not bend or break for a very long time.
A pair of inscribed stone daggers

<LoreItalics>What is time to us? We stand outside. All things have happened. All things are happening.</> - Unknown

These daggers appear to have been created by a madman and inscribed a language unknown to men. Only an oracle, high on the fumes of yellow lotus, claims to have been able to read the text inscribed on them. It reads: 'In the cradle of the Nameless Days, the leopard of the smoking mirror shall eat the moon and sun. There is no beginning. There is no end. Invisible mouths devoured them, from either side, as a prelude to a hideous kiss. You will see them in time.'

Light attacks with these daggers seem to take no effort, but heavy attacks seem to weary the wielder even more.
A pair of knives forged in Zhaibar

<LoreItalics>The governor checked his motion toward the sword on the table. He was within reach of the yard-long Zhaibar knife that glittered in the intruder's fist, and he knew the desperate quickness of a hillman.</> - People of the Black Circle

It is not known whether it is some special quality to the metal forged in Zhaibar, or if it is simply the training that they give their warriors, but all know that the wielder of a Zhaibar blade is to be feared.

<LoreItalics>Even as he struck, the apparition vanished, and his blade clashed deafeningly on the adamantine surface. Instantly he sensed something abnormal. The blade stuck to the table! He wrenched at it savagely. It did not give. This was no mesmeristic trick. The table was a giant magnet.</> - Shadows in Zamboula

In Zamboula, at the shrine of Hanuman, there is a table that attracts metal objects. The faithful consider it a divine object, and they claim that anything that touches it inherits a part of the divinity temporarily. 

This blade is made of the same material as that table and, though it is hard to explain, this blade weighs nothing. It seems to repel the very ground itself and push upwards, against the hands of the bearer.
A sword borne by the Adventurers of Nemedia

<LoreItalics>I was riding for Belverus on Amalric's business, said the Adventurer, advancing warily. The starlight was a long sheen on the great two-handed sword he bore naked in his hand.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

Considered the most dangerous foes in all of Nemedia, the Adventurers are a class of warrior peculiar to that country. They have not attained the wealth and position of knighthood or have fallen from that estate; they are hard-bitten fighters, dedicating their lives to war and adventure. They hold themselves accountable to no man but the king.

At first glance, this sword appears impossible, the blade a paper-thin sheet of metal that looks like it would bend and break at the slightest contact.

Instead, the sword is incredibly formidable against armored opponents, being able to slide into the gaps and crevices in armor with the greatest of ease.

The only disadvantage to the thinness of the blade is that it becomes more difficult to sheath, meaning that those who do not pay attention will find themselves with a thin, deadly cut on the inside of their thighs.
A great sword that glows and hums

This sword once belonged to the great troubadour, Jedias Manbaebe, who travelled the known kingdoms telling great sagas about a group of monks who fought evil knights a long time ago in a land far, far away.

During his shows, he would act out the battles using this sword, causing gasps from the crowd as he swung its glowing length back and forth as it hummed in the night.

Unfortunately, as the legend of his sword grew, two bandits (Dis and Knee) took an interest. They ambushed him one day, and took his sword, but were disgusted to discover that the sword was just an ordinary sword smeared with glowing paste and with a concealed noisemaker.

They stabbed Jedias with his own sword and left him to rot.

This sword does very little when equipped but make noises and light.
A two-handed blade with a single purpose

This sword was crafted to serve as a simple blade for a watchman in the ancient kingdom of Valusia. Over the years, it was passed down, watchman to watchman, and the hilt was rebound, but the blade was never repaired.

Eventually, Valusia disappeared and the watchmen were gone, and the blade was forgotten.

When it was rediscovered, it was rusted and pitted by age, but it could still be swung in battle. 

Any attempts to remove the rust and stains are futile, but the weapon itself is as sturdy and steadfast as its name.
A mace that swings with great force

This mace is forged of a metal that defies common description. It is heavy and ponderous to lift and swing, but when it connects it does so with bone-breaking force.

The massive amount that it weighs is a small tradeoff for the damage that it does to foes.
A club that refuses to kill

This crude club once belonged to Sergius of Khrosha who, before he became a captain, was the first-mate of a ship called The Beast. Sergius had one job when the ship was in port - to waylay drunken soldiers and drag them back to The Beast.

For that purpose, he used the club he knew affectionately as Lovetap.

Perhaps it was some combination of materials, or perhaps it was some bizarre sorcerous trait, but either way, the club became extremely good at knocking people out - but it would not damage them beyond that.

Eventually, Sergius lost the club in a gambling den, and Lovetap dropped out of sight and mind.

This club deals only concussion damage to enemies.
A club that imparts terrible strength on its wielder

<LoreItalics>Conan rose, still smiling, as if to reach into a near-by cooking pot; then quick as a cat he struck Aja a terrible blow with the heavy bone. The Bakalah war-chief slumped over, his skull crushed in, and instantly a frightful yell rent the skies as the Bamulas went into action like blood-mad panthers.</> - The Vale of Lost Women

The Bakalah who live on the border of Kush are known for their fearsome raids to take slaves and other captives. And none were more feared than Aja, their war-chief, a great brute of a man who was deadly with both club and spear.

This bony club was allegedly used to kill Aja in a moment of betrayal by a neighboring tribe.
Fokove ces he fo lojani rudab gerere ta yi rofibu.

Oro se limetah de yacie rer ned dofat tihot leci. Jiso toku tetes yoqic itak lienan enapet bito? Bupi icarimir hal pe opine davec lu. Te totid yitijel pemepa nolon gisi tiefielit nabel. Pa ecoticel tetola totuhir tanielod ra alo lida? Ditemit na birig.

Burusier igiweper fa roc losor mimecieb. Butara henile reg he ha lobo leru nape anilinor hat! Si pep otep lefuno usi. Lasec hecapah reterad ric hoh: Zaw eneranaj ro taso asat nerinah royogi: Nienasic inosine sin, cinoc ieri ciyet tote bunate rie tem. Ne enosem hopehi cipacih teruso veso omenigo afelo nuhilad ho.
A mace that seems to break constantly

This mace evokes a legendary amount of swearing in the wielder and their enemies alike. When it strikes, it does massive damage, causing foes to curse it with every blow. But alas, it also falls apart constantly, requiring regular repair and often, during battle, leaving its owner without a weapon.

A bastard it is, and a bastard it will always be.

When this weapon was forged, it was left too long in the coals, becoming super-heated until it glowed a fierce, white-gold.

Once it was cooled and fitted, the new owner noticed that it still glimmered in the darkness, even when there were no other lights around. Unfortunately for the owner, who was a footpad by trade, the light interfered with business that is mostly done in dark alleys. The weapon was quickly sold on, and has changed hands dozens of times, yet it still maintains its glow.

<LoreItalics>He knew the hideous habits of the priests of the East and was aware that an invader of Hanuman's shrine might expect to encounter almost any sort of nightmare horror.</> - Shadows in Zamboula

The worship of Hanuman migrated to the west from Vendhya, and as it brought with it military traditions of Vendhyan origin. This particular gada is extremely large and is reputed to have been wielded by Hanuman himself once upon a time.

The oversized head makes it heavy and awkward to swing, but it does a lot of damage when it lands a blow.
A Warhammer which combines hammer and pick

There is no love lost between the Knights of Poitain and the Zingarans who live just to their south across the border. The Zingarans raid the rich lands of Poitain and the knights take revenge by crossing the border and burning ever crop and field that they see.

The Bec-de-Corbin was developed by a wily Zingaran fighter who wished to be able to more easily penetrate the armor of his Poitanian foes. Copies of the weapon quickly spread southward, along with word of its effectiveness.

<LoreItalics>Even as he struck, the apparition vanished, and his blade clashed deafeningly on the adamantine surface. Instantly he sensed something abnormal. The blade stuck to the table! He wrenched at it savagely. It did not give. This was no mesmeristic trick. The table was a giant magnet.</> - Shadows in Zamboula

In Zamboula, at the shrine of Hanuman, there is a table that attracts metal objects. The faithful consider it a divine object, and they claim that anything that touches it inherits a part of the divinity temporarily. 

This hammer is made of the same material as that table and, though it is hard to explain, this hammer weighs nothing. It seems to repel the very ground itself and push upwards, against the hands of the bearer.

<LoreItalics>Of this Kothian wizard dark tales were told; tousle-headed women in northern and western villages frightened children with his name, and rebellious slaves were brought to abased submission quicker than by the lash, with threat of being sold to him. Men said that he had a whole library of dark works bound in skin flayed from living human victims, and that in nameless pits below the hill whereon his palace sat, he trafficked with the powers of darkness, trading screaming girl slaves for unholy secrets.</> - The Scarlet Citadel

There is a tale told that when the pits beneath the palace of Tsotha-lanti were being created, the work fell behind schedule. Tsotha-lanti demanded to know the reason for the delay and the trembling slave explained that they had encountered stone beneath the earth that was resistant to their hammers, which kept shattering on the hard stone.

Tsotha slew the unfortunate slave, and then passed the rest of the work gangs hammers through the blood, muttering an incantation. From that point onwards, the hammers smashed the stone easily and never seemed to chip or break.

When the work was complete, the hammers used disappeared and how they came to be where they are today is unknown.
A Hyrkanian bow with remarkable accuracy

Across the Vilayet, where the blue sea gives way to the steppes, the Hyrkanians live in the saddle from the day that they are born - learning to shoot, fight and eat.

This bow was crafted for the son of a great khan, but the boy was trampled by bulls before he was ten years old and the old khan was left with nothing but the bow in memory of his favored son.

The old khan claimed that the bow would whisper to him with the voice of his son, telling him where to find water and how to avoid enemies. The Khan's other sons saw this as a sign of their father being unfit to rule, and promptly knifed him in the back.

The bow was given away, or lost, or sold. And the son of the khan was forgotten.
A bow that requires great strength to draw

In Ophir lives a pretty lass,
With hair of shining gold,
her rounded breasts and supple ass,
would make a weak man bold.

Her suitors came from all the world,
expectin' to be shunned,
But Bessie was a gen'rous girl,
She did them, every one!

All day and night they heard the cries,
Of Bessie in her bed,
And men were dropping off like flies,
She'd ridden 'em to dead.

Now came the Priest of Mitra,
And the girl he did beseech,
Stop with all this wickedness,
Just listen to me preach

But Bessie was a peacemaker,
She didn't want to fight,
She acted as a horse breaker,
And rode that priest all night.

The priest would not be beaten back,
His heart would not give way,
Though Bessie sought to drain his sack,
He'd shoot throughout the day.

And then together they each found,
The one that they had sought,
In marriage were they solemn bound,
Together they were caught.

The priest and girl they took their vow,
And shaved their hair away,
Let this be used to string a bow,
And may it shoot all day!
A bow that seems to penetrate even the thickest armor

There was a legend among the Nordheimers that one of the skalds was captured by a Hyperborean Witch-man. 

The skald was imprisoned in the top of a Hyperborean keep, where thick icicles hung from the ceiling and the cold northern winds would cut him directly to the bone. He was going to die, so he prayed to Ymir for help.

The Skald had just given up hope, when a flash of lightning outside the tower illuminated his room - and revealed the shape of a bow trapped inside one of the icicles.

Chipping slowly at the icicle, the Skald uncovered the wondrous bow, and shaped himself some arrows of ice from the shards.
The next time his captor came to feed him, he shot an ice arrow at the Hyperborean, expecting it to shatter on his chest. Instead, it passed through the armor and directly into the creature's heart.

The Skald escaped, and the bow went with him.
A bow that fires arrows which always break

A peasant from Koth was tired of mercenary troops riding across his fields on their way to war. He went out to confront them, with a simple bow made of a bent branch and arrows of simple twigs.

They laughed when he politely asked them to ride around his fields. One of them kicked him into the mud.

Humiliated, he levelled his bow at the leader. And fired. The twig flew straight and true, striking the mercenary leader in the breastplate, right above his heart.

The twig shattered, but before the mercenaries could react, a sharp splinter flew up and lodged itself it the mercenary leader's eye.

They slaughtered the peasant, of course. But the bow somehow made it to the Exiled Lands.

This bow cannot penetrate armor at all, but it does very high damage on impact.
A legendary bow that boosts accuracy

When the Lemurians fled their islands, they were captured and enslaved by the mysterious race that lived on the eastern shores of the Thurian continent.

A remnant of a remnant escaped that slavery and crossed the world in search of succor.

Thousands of people, weary and terrified, needed to be protected and fed as they crossed hostile kingdoms, ghost-haunted moors and the jungles full of dangerous creatures.

A group of women, known as Dagon's Daughters, volunteered to protect the group. They were experts with the bow, and agile fighters at close range.

This bow, simply known as The Huntress, once belonged to Dagon's Daughters.
A legendary shield with an interesting strap mechanism

Black Bruargh was not always a bandit. In his life before the Border Kingdoms, he was an armorer and blacksmith. He was inventive and liked to try out new designs for shields and weapons.

More often than not, his designs failed, leading to the deaths of those who bought his goods. This led to a drop in custom, so he was forced to close his doors.

Ironically, the last thing he had worked on was a specialized shield with straps that gave the wielder more freedom of movement during battle. His theory was that it would allow for more flexibility in combat.

Black Bruargh left the shield, along with all his other inventions, closed his shop, and went on to become one of the most feared bandits in the history of the Border Kingdom.

His debtors sold all of his inventions.

<LoreItalics>Thrusting his dagger-point into the crack, Conan exerted leverage with a corded forearm. The blade bent, but it was of unbreakable Akbitanan steel.</> - Jewels of Gwaluhr

The expertise of the smiths of Akbitana combined with a local source of ore that has special qualities, provides the hardest steel weapon on earth.

Usually only sold in the city itself, this shield is a very rare find.

<LoreItalics>In the swirling red chaos a terrible apparition suddenly appeared before Conan's rearing steed. It was prince Kutamun, naked but for a loin-cloth, his harness hacked away, his crested helmet dented, his limbs splashed with blood.</> - Black Colossus

Prince Kutamun of Stygia is a legendarily fearless warrior. His savage fury is well known among his subjects and he is rumored to be invincible in battle.

This shield, however, has never seen battle. Prince Kutamun does not deign to use a shield in battle and, despite the effort that his mother went to have this forged to keep her darling child safe, he refuses to use it.

This hurt the feelings of his overprotective mother. 

Don't blame me when somebody stabs you to death with a dagger then! she told him, tossing the shield on a rubbish pile, where it was promptly stolen by an urchin.

Mist clings to the surface of this shield and chills the arm of any who hold it.  Nothing is known of who crafted the shield, or what strange sorceries cause it to remain chilly on even the warmest of days.

Just some runes in ancient Atlantean, spelling out the name.

Equipping this shield gives a boost to heat protection.

Warmth emanates from the surface of this shield and heats the arm of any who hold it.  Nothing is known of who crafted the shield, or by what strange sorceries it remains warm on even the coldest of days.

Just some runes in ancient Atlantean, spelling out the name. Equipping this shield gives a boost to cold protection.
A warspear forged on Mount Yimsha

<LoreItalics>Like a man in a trance the warrior thrust the butt of his spear against the base of the wall, and placed the keen head against his body, just below the ribs. Then slowly, stolidly, he leaned against it with all his weight, so that it transfixed his body and came out between his shoulders. Sliding down the shaft he lay still, the spear jutting above him its full length, like a horrible stalk growing out of his back.</> - People of the Black Circle

The Master of the Black Circle is a reclusive and mysterious figure, feared by all who dwell in the region of Mount Yimsha. The locals avoid the mountain as much as possible and few who venture up the winding path ever return to speak of it.

This spear, then, is an anomaly. How it came to be is unknown, whether it was forged on the mountain or brought wholesale into being via sorcery.

It has excellent balance in battle, allowing heavy swings at a fraction of their regular stamina cost.
A pike pitted with rust ravaged by age

Gavain was a member of the Free Companies, a red-handed mercenary who fought and plundered wherever he was commanded. He earned considerable fame during a border skirmish between two Shemitish city-states when he defended a corridor against a surging rush of men.

Shortly afterwards, however, he was struck down by the one ailment for which there is no cure - love. He followed a golden-haired Aesir warrioress into the north, abandoning his gear which, according to mercenary legend, rusted overnight.

Nothing is known of the fate of Gavain of his gear, though it is still said of any mercenary who abandons the companies for a woman that they have been touched by Gavain's pike.
A pike from the legendary Black Dragons

The Black Dragons are the elite troops of Aquilonia, charged with guarding the Royal family of Aquilonia until death. They are well respected throughout Tarantia and the realm, and the king sends them to serve his justice to bandits and other outlaws.

With such a towering reputation, only the best of recruits and the most valuable equipment are ever used to outfit the troops.

This pike was forged by a master smith in Aquilonia itself.
A pike used by Turanian warlords

The Turanian army is feared throughout the west for their ever-expanding grasp and long-standing plans of conquest. There is a sense of impending doom over every kingdom that stands like a bulwark, border to border, with Turan.

When the Turanians conquer a city, they offer a single chance to surrender. If refused, they are without mercy, killing every man, woman and child. If they are accepted, they simply impale the city leaders outside the gates, as a reminder not to test their authority.

This pike was specially designed to impale enemies.
A pike with an easily bendable shaft

This pike is, at first glance, completely normal. It is only when using it in battle, one notices that the haft has an extreme amount of flex.

These were originally designed in Khitai as training spears for the monks who followed Yun, the god of death. The flexible haft was used to perform death defying leaps over the spiked, burning sacrifice pits that burn outside the main temple building in Paikang.
An axe coated in strange substance

The axe has long been a staple of the Red Brotherhood who terrorize the Turanian vessels that travel on the Vilayet.

The axes are coated in an alchemical substance that dampens their ability to strike sparks on metal, to prevent accidental fires during ship to ship combat.

This axe, when equipped, is more effective at penetrating armor.
A legendary axe from the Black Kingdoms

For centuries, traders in Kush would hear tales of a holy relic known simply as the Axe of the Lion. It was kept in the palace of El Shebbeh for a century, displayed only to the most honored guests of the kingdom.

Then, the axe went missing. All of Shumballah was put on alert and the Chagas and Gallahs were at each other's throats over the theft.

Which was exactly as Shevatas the thief had planned it. He took ship for Zingara while the locals were squabbling and offered it for auction on the docks of Kordava. It was purchased by a local noble and it passed out of sight and mind for many years.
A glowing axe with a wicked edge

For years, Glimmermoon was the favored weapon of the Royal Executioner of Nemedia. The executioner himself was a Hyperborean, a gaunt, raw-boned fellow who brought the axe with him from his native land. The axe earned its name due to its glowing metal and half-moon shape. Nobody recalls the name of the executioner.

His executions were quite the show, his glowing axe whirling in a great arc to lop the head from the guilty. But he fell afoul of a plot to overthrow the throne, and his axe went missing in the ensuing turmoil.
The signature axe of a team of heroes

Berserkers have long been known in the northern kingdoms for their absolute, unflinching ferocity. Some have suggested that their berserk rages are the result of chewing a particularly potent form of mushroom.

This axe looks familiar. Thought it is not easy to place it, the shape of the blade, the width of the haft and even the smell of the metal are like old friends.

Carrying this axe is like having an old friend around, together anything can be overcome.
A pick made out of obsidian, hard enough to mine anything

<LoreItalics>'I know him not,' he answered. 'He is mad to say I hired him. Let him take his just desserts. He has a strong back and the toil in the mines will be well for him.'</> - The God in the Bowl

The pick is one of the simplest tools known to man. Used extensively in mines across Hyboria to split rocks and, if necessary, split heads.

Created in the fires at the burning heart of the forge and wrought in ornate patterns as it cooled, this pick is strong and durable. It almost seems a shame to waste it on rocks.
An axe of obsidian for chopping wood

<LoreItalics> The rest were toilers, without armor save for shirts of toughened leather, but they were brawny stalwarts, and skilled in the use of their hunting bows, woodsmen's axes, and boar-spears.</> - The Black Stranger

One need only see the smoke curling from the chimneys of hamlets across the Thurian continent to understand the ubiquity of the humble hatchet. 

Gathering wood for cooking and construction are a part of daily life and the hatchet serves admirably for this purpose. Primarily used to hack down trees and fallen logs, hatchets can also be used in combat though they make unwieldy weapons.

<LoreItalics>The blade glinted in the starlight, and blood spurted.</> - The Man-Eaters of Zamboula

Sickles are one-handed tools sporting a crescent-shaped blade. Made for harvesting crops, such a tool can just as easily sheer flesh and bone and reap a bloody bounty.
A javelin in a blasphemous ancient style

<LoreItalics>And at last mankind conquered, so long ago that naught but dim legends come to us through the ages. The snake-people were the last to go, yet at last men conquered even them and drove them forth into the waste lands of the world, there to mate with true snakes until some day, say the sages, the horrid breed shall vanish utterly.</> - The Shadow Kingdom

The snake-people were thought to be gone. First defeated in the war with first man at the dawn of time, then purged again by King Kull of Valusia.

But here, in this bizarre, mysterious piece of the world, they found succor with the Giant-kings. Perhaps the city in the volcano was ancient before even the Giant-kings lived in this land. But either way, the degenerate remnant remains.
A javelin with a head of obsidian

The javelin is one of the most versatile weapons of the Hyborian age. 
It is light enough to be thrown with some degree of accuracy. Enemies fleeing a battle are almost always surprised to find three feet of spear jutting from between their shoulder blades.
A bow reinforced with Star Metal

<LoreItalics> A long bow and a strong bow, and let the sky grow dark! The cord to the nock, the shaft to the ear, and the king of Koth for a mark!</>
Song of the Bossonian Archers.

In trained hands, bows are lethal weapons that can bring down a foe from afar. A large part of the versatility of the bow comes from the arrows used in battle.

This bow will be able to bring down both human and non-human foes, but it relies heavily on the skill of the wielder.
A bow reinforced with Hardened Steel

Song of the Bossonian Archers.

This bow will be able to bring down both human and non-human foes, but it relies heavily on the skill of the wielder.
A long spear in the style of sunken Lemuria

<LoreItalics>Then the Cataclysm rocked the world. Atlantis and Lemuria sank, and the Pictish Islands were heaved up to form the mountain peaks of a new continent.</> - The Hyborian Age

With superior reach the pike is a common weapon on the battlefields of Hyboria. The most effective use of the pike is from behind the lines of battle, thrusting into the gaps in a shield wall.

The Lemurians were an island people, inhabiting an island chain off the eastern coast of the Thurian continent - until their kingdom sank beneath the waves. Their story took a brutal turn when they landed on the eastern coastline - and were promptly enslaved by the race of people who dwelt there.

What Lemurian artefacts are doing here is a mystery. Just like the Exiled Lands themselves.
A sword in the style of sunken Lemuria

<LoreItalics>Then the Cataclysm rocked the world. Atlantis and Lemuria sank, and the Pictish Islands were heaved up to form the mountain peaks of a new continent.</> - The Hyborian Age

Swords are straight-bladed, one-handed weapons, both fast and reliable.

A two-handed sword of Acheronian make

<LoreItalics>'I pay my way with steel!' roared the man in armor, brandishing the great sword that glittered bluely in the sun.</> - Queen of the Black Coast

Great swords are faster than many other two-handed weapons, and their great reach makes them ideal for fending off groups of opponents.

This weapon is forged in the style of ancient Acheron, a kingdom of sorcerers that dominated the northern kingdoms over three thousand years ago. Scholars have noted that the Acheronian style bears a striking similarity to that of the mysterious pre-human race that once ruled what is modern-day Stygia.
A rudimentary shield of loosely bound branches

<LoreItalics> Presently the intention of the pirates became apparent to all, as a group of some thirty men advanced, pushing before them a great shield made out of the planks from the boats, and the timbers of the boat-house itself.</> - The Black Stranger

Most warriors prefer to carry a shield into battle if there is one available. The best blow is the one that misses, but the second best blow is the one that you block.

This shield is a primitive bundle of branches, strapped together with rudimentary twine made from plant fibres. It will shatter under sustained blows, but it might be the difference between life and death.
A shield lashed together from the bones of the dead

<LoreItalics> Wildly driven spears and knives glanced from his helmet or the shield on his left arm, while his broadsword cleft flesh and bone, split skulls, scattered brains and spilled entrails into the bloody dust.</> - The Snout in the Dark

Bones lashed to a wooden frame make for an intimidating defensive wall. Unfortunately, the brittle nature of bone means that intimidation is the strongest element of this shield. A few blows and it will shatter and leave the wielder vulnerable.

A sturdy targe of wooden planks reinforced with iron

<LoreItalics> Shields crashed against shields, and between them spears drove in and blood spurted.</> - Black Colossus

A round shield, reinforced with metal around the rim and leather straps for ease of holding. It is not uncommon to cover the front of the targe with a sheet of leather or hide and decorate it with patterns.

The targe is a shield designed for attack as much as defence. A well placed strike with the shield can stagger an enemy and leave them open to attacks from a weapon in the main hand.

At first glance, this mace seems very primitive. On closer inspection, however, a remarkable amount of care has been put into sharpening the jagged edges of it, enabling it to shred, rather than bash, through most armors.
Mastercrafted in the eastern kingdoms, the metal used to forge blade with has been folded several million times. It is the epitome of craftsmanship, infused with the very soul of its creator.

This shield is crafted from the hardened carapace of the Scorpion Queen. It is strong and extremely durable.

This hammer has an inlaid core of solid metal and as such is incredibly heavy and cumbersome to swing. However - impacts from this hammer has the additional effect of sapping the stamina from its target.
These daggers look mundane enough. However, upon closer inspection, you may notice tiny serrations in the blade.

<LoreItalics>'I pay my way with steel!' roared the man in armor, brandishing the great sword that glittered bluely in the sun.</> - Queen of the Black Coast

Great swords are faster than many other two-handed weapons, and their great reach makes them ideal for fending off groups of opponents.

This weapon was found in a grave and has rusted. However - even now - the blade strikes true and strong.
A targe covered by iron shielding

<LoreItalics> In ecstasy warriors clashed their notched swords on their riven shields, and the people of the town, ragged beggars and rich merchants, harlots in red kirtles and dames in silks and satins, fell to their knees and cried out for joy to Mitra, tears of gratitude streaming down their faces. </> - The Scarlet Citadel

Strengthened with iron, this targe sacrifices some of its manoeuvrability for additional durability. The knobs on the front of the shield are designed to notch the weapons and claws of foes. 

The rivets and design work do not point to a particular cultural tradition, but rather reflect the experimental nature of smith work in the Exiled Lands.

The targe is a shield designed for attack as much as defence. A well placed strike with the shield can stagger an enemy and leave them open to attacks from a weapon in the main hand.
A pick caked in black blood

<LoreItalics>'I know him not,' he answered. 'He is mad to say I hired him. Let him take his just desserts. He has a strong back and the toil in the mines will be well for him.'</> - The God in the Bowl

The pick is one of the simplest tools known to man. Used extensively in mines across Hyboria to split rocks and, if necessary, split heads.

The blood caked onto the obsidian edge has etched and hardened this tool.
A hatchet caked in black blood

<LoreItalics> The rest were toilers, without armor save for shirts of toughened leather, but they were brawny stalwarts, and skilled in the use of their hunting bows, woodsmen's axes, and boar-spears.</> - The Black Stranger

One need only see the smoke curling from the chimneys of hamlets across the Thurian continent to understand the ubiquity of the humble hatchet. 

The blood caked onto the obsidian edge has etched and hardened this tool.
A sickle caked in black blood

<LoreItalics>The blade glinted in the starlight, and blood spurted.</> - The Man-Eaters of Zamboula

Sickles are one-handed tools sporting a crescent-shaped blade. Made for harvesting crops, such a tool can just as easily sheer flesh and bone and reap a bloody bounty.

The blood caked onto the obsidian edge has etched and hardened this tool.
A skinning knife caked in black blood

<LoreItalics>There's more than one way of skinning a panther.</> - Red Nails

Any warrior will tell you that a dagger balanced for battle is not designed to be used for skinning animals, though it will do in a pinch.
This skinning knife has a sharpened edge designed to easily split tendon, scrape flesh and free hides in a single piece. 

Using such a knife has the advantage of providing more hides with less effort.

The blood caked onto the obsidian edge has etched and hardened this tool.
A heater shield of beaten steel

<LoreItalics> The Stygians had discarded their bows; helmeted heads bent to the blast, dark eyes glaring over the rims of their shields, they came on in an inexorable surge, striding over their fallen comrades.</> Black Collossus

Usable by both infantry and cavalry, the heater shield is known for its unique shape and large area of protection.

As a defensive material, there is very little than can match the quality of steel. The additional weight is worth the extra protection.
A large shield with a slot for a lantern

<LoreItalics> Arus stood in a vast corridor, lighted by huge candles in niches along the walls. These walls were hung with black velvet tapestries, and between the tapestries hung shields and crossed weapons of fantastic make.</> - The God in the Bowl

Shields traditionally serve a single purpose defense. The lantern shield attempts to broaden that definition, however, by providing adventurers with a series of options for both attack and defense.

Developed in Argos, this small shield was originally designed to protect the watchmen of that city as they went about their nightly rounds, providing them with a handy light source for the darkest alleyways and corners of the city. However, the wily gladiators of Messantian fighting pits soon saw that the focused light of the lanterns mounted on the shield could be used to bedazzle and confuse their foes especially in the darkness.

Lantern shields come in many designs, from buckler shapes with jutting sword breakers and attached gauntlets, to simply large shield with an enclosure for holding the lantern that gives the shield its name.
A whispering shield forged from an ancient design

<LoreItalics> I am cursed. A fiend from the abysses has set his mark upon me. Night after night he lurks in the shadows, whispering awful secrets to me.</> - Black Colossus

This shield was created from designs looted in the unnamed city ruins within the Exiled Lands. The design of the shield is intricate, with a serpentlike design that is both repellent and fascinating when examined.
This shield is heavy but the solid construction offers additional protection against repeated blows. 

When equipped, this shield seems to whisper to its bearer in the long forgotten language of the Giant-Kings. This constant distraction drains the willpower of the user, but those who master it may uncover hidden strengths.

<LoreItalics>The Stygians had discarded their bows; helmeted heads bent to the blast, dark eyes glaring over the rims of their shields, they came on in an inexorable surge, striding over their fallen comrades.'</> - Black Colossus

This ornamental shield, usually used by Stygian soldiers in ceremonial parade, is strong enough to offer formidable protection against attacks. The ridges and ornamentations provide an advantage in battle, catching the blades of the enemy as they slide along the rim while allowing full visibility of the enemy.

Ceremonial versions of this shield are usually wrought in brass and gold, but the more practical versions use tinted iron and steel.
A ceremonial shield dedicated to Set

<LoreItalics>These walls were hung with black velvet tapestries, and between the tapestries hung shields and crossed weapons of fantastic make.</> - The God in the Bowl

Among the rituals of the cult of Set, is the ability to render special properties into base metals. In particular, gold is much favored by the priests of Set to be used in the creation of these divine shields, which they claim will offer the blessings of Set.

Some have pointed out that the process which hardens the gold darkens it almost to the color of bronze, and that the specialized priests who perform the process often move on quickly to new cities and villages. But not too loudly. That would be blasphemous.
A hardened steel shield of Cimmerian make

<LoreItalics>Through a whistling cloud of arrows they plowed to break like a thundering wave on the bristling wall of spears and shields.</> - The Hour of the Dragon

This hardened steel shield bears the swirling markings of a Cimmerian clan.

These daggers, crafted in worship of the god Zath, are symbolic representations of the purifying venom of Zath. They tear and rend flesh with the same enthusiasm as the spider god himself.

Daggers are a weapon used with passion by the untrained and with a cold dispassion by the trained. Unseasoned warriors consider swords the superior weapon - until they come across a master, twin blades flashing as they dash and dart within the reach of their enemies and disembowel them.
A longspear affixed with a fang of Zath

The distinction between a dagger and a shortsword is blurry at best. The topic has been of much speculation among the smiths of Ahkbitan for many, many years - often discussed over tankards of ale in backwater taverns.

The conclusion of those drunken debates is this - if you'd use it to eat a meal or slit a throat, it qualifies as a dagger or knife - if you'd use it to stab somebody in the face, it is probably a shortsword.
A shield crafted from the remains of the Abysmal Remnant

<LoreItalics>He saw and knew the ancient and evil serpent which swayed there, its wedge-shaped head, and its palely gleaming barrel rippling out behind it. A forked tongue darted in and out, and the firelight glittered on bared fangs.</> - Beyond the Black River

Staring long enough into the eye of the Abysmal Remnant, embedded in this shield, fills the mind with bizarre images.

Once, the Priestking made a pact with a demon from the outer void to inhabit some formed flesh that he was crafting. This was to be a weapon, used in the war against the human city in the north.

The experiment failed, the creature was born limbless, and the experiment was abandoned. An acolyte of the Priestking tossed it into the sewer system to drown in The Dregs.

But the creature did not die, and the demon was not freed. It found a pool where it could excrete the acid that it needed to survive. And then it reached out with its mind, looking for food.

Over time, it grew and the rats and other vermin in the sewers were no longer enough to sustain it...

With superior reach the pike is a common weapon on the battlefields of Hyboria. The most effective use of the pike is from behind the lines of battle, thrusting into the gaps in a shield wall.

Stygian hunters carry great broad-headed pikes to kill off the larger creatures that they encounter a commonly used but incredibly dangerous tactic is to goad the creature into charging while bracing the pike against the ground.

The thick haft and weighted end mean that the pike must be wielded in two hands.

<LoreItalics> Well, the folk of the city can't help us just now. And they might not, if they could. The people of the Black Countries are generally hostile to strangers. Probably stick us full of spears.</> - Red Nails

This pike is heavy on one end and difficult to aim. The scavenged materials used in its manufacture will deteriorate quickly, making this a thrust-and-bust weapon.

The thick haft and weighted end mean that the pike must be wielded in two hands.

<LoreItalics> Spears! he muttered. What a blasted fool I am not to have thought of that before! That shows what a pretty woman does to a man's mind.</> - Red Nails

Originally used for fishing along the Argossean coastline, the flamboyant gladiator Aros of Koth decided to adopt the trident as his signature weapon.

The extremely broad head of the weapon makes it top heavy and too thick to be used in a shield wall while the barbed prongs are prone to getting caught on armor and flesh. 

The trident is best used against large creatures where stopping power is more important than precision. Aros of Koth discovered this the hard way, earning renown and fortune for taking down the Beast Lizard of Messantia, but then being killed in a later encounter with a swarm of Darfari Cannibals.
A spear with a head forged from mysterious star metal

This impossibly sharp spear has a head made of legendary star metal, the work of a master craftsman.

Spears are two-handed weapons with an ungainly tall wooden haft, but their reach is second to none.

Star metal is rare, smelted from ore that falls from the heavens. Weapons made from such material are preternaturally powerful.

Hardened steel, finely wrought, forms the head of this large spear baring the swirling markings of a Cimmerian clan.

The Cimmerians make large, two-handed spears for maximum reach to hunt the most dangerous game animals. Such weapons are fine to have against more human opponents as well.

Shaped of steel and marked with the swirling markings of a Cimmerian clan, this battle-axe is sharp, durable and capable of inflicting vicious wounds.

Battle-axes are a difficult weapon for inexperienced warriors, due to their smaller surface area and uneven balance. No other one-handed weapon shares their raw power, and they can wreak havoc on unarmored foes.

Cimmerian clans often engage in violent local conflict and the battle-axe is a preferred weapon for breaching the wood-walled settlements and laying waste to the rival clansmen within.

<LoreItalics> Across the sea of heads and spears Conan's madmen saw Amalric's riders forging steadily through the rout, to the rise and fall of axes and maces, and a mad joy of victory exalted each man's heart and made his arm steel.</> - Black Colossus

Though it bears no makers-mark, this mace is excellently balanced and made of strong steel.

In primitive cultures, short swords are scoffed at as little more than knives. However, in the Hyborian cultures such as Aquilonia or Nemedia, where shield walls and cavalry charges have become a reality of combat, short swords are prized for their ability to thrust and stab in spaces where no longsword could ever be wielded.

A typical footsoldier in the armies of Aquilonia will carry a spear and a short sword along with their shield - and when the initial charge of battle is over and the slow roll of the meat grinder begins, it is short swords that decide the day.

Because they are smaller and weigh less than other weapons, short swords are also faster to use and consume less stamina than their larger counterparts.

Once, the Priestking made a pact with a demon from the outer void to inhabit some formed flesh that he was crafting. This was to be a weapon, used in the war against the human city in the north.

The experiment failed, the creature was born limbless and the experiment was abandoned. An acolyte of the Priestking tossed it into the sewer system, to drown in The Dregs.

But the creature did not die, and the demon was not freed. It found a pool where it could excrete the acid that it needed to survive. And then it reached out with its mind, looking for food.

When the sand whips and swirls in the wind, abrading everything in its path, even the smallest amount of protection is appreciated.
This tunic provides little protection from sword or fang, but it does provide slight relief from cold, heat and stinging sand.

Digging in the gritty soil of the Exiled Lands and tearing up plants by their roots without protection is dirty, infection-prone work. 
These handwraps provide some protection from the elements and physical attacks.

In the Hyborian age, nudity is a part of life. In warm climates, men and women go bare chested and wear flimsy clothing, slaves are clothed in whatever tatters they can find and children run naked in the streets.
Clothing, however, is a practical bulwark against the elements. And these leggings, coarse as they may be, can protect some very sensitive areas from the elements.
The soles of these footwraps offer very poor protection from the sharp-edged stones that litter the ground of the Exiled Lands.

Across the Hyborian kingdoms and beyond, in every village in every province, the smith is a necessity in daily life. From blades to ploughsnares, blacksmiths craft the tools and weapons to feed and arm the population.
In every village or town, the Blacksmith is recognized by their uniform - this simple leather apron. Offering protection from errant sparks and pockets for storing small tools, this apron is as much a badge of craft as the smiths hammer or the forge itself.
Thick leather gloves offering crafting protection

These gloves are made of thick leather molded over a padded inside. Made to protect the hands from damage while working with dangerous crafting elements, they offer a small amount of protection in combat.
As a secondary usage, the heavy gloves can be donned and worn during brawls to avoid damaging the hands in combat.
One famous sailor, known only as Dorgan of the Python, makes a large sum of gold by fighting his way across the Vilayet sea and betting on his own fights. He claims that the gloves keep his prize possessions safe.
Shemitish turban commonly worn in the meadowland cities

The meadowland cities of western Shem thrive on the trade that comes with the caravans that pass into Turan and Khitai. Due to their access to these caravans, the Shemitish people often have access to the first pick of goods coming from the east - including fine silks from Khitai and brightly dyed cloth from Turan. This bounty of cloth is reflected in the loose fitting, comfortable clothing woven by the tailors of Shem.
This clothing is a practical bulwark against the elements but won't be enough to stop a blade.

A pair of bone earrings often worn by Vanir commoners

As the massive glaciers of the north expand and move southward, the kingdoms of Asgard and Vanaheim are pushed slowly southward. This, in part, contributes to the perception of the Vanir and Aesir as warlike people - they are continually looking to the south in search of new lands to settle. 

Thus not all Vanir that are encountered in the north are raiders and warriors, quite often the weary adventurer will stumble across a caravan of Vanir settlers, looking for fertile lands to settle their new clan.

These earrings provide no significant protection, but they are marked with clan symbols - so that if a dead settler is found, their possessions can be returned to the clan. Jokingly referred to by the Aesir as Vanearrings.

The application of symbols and paints to the body during war is a time honored tradition of the Nordheimers. In days past, tattoos were traditional, but the ever-shifting tides of battle and alliance between those war-like tribes made it difficult to be certain who would be friend or foe in the future.

One well known tale tells of a chieftain's son, married off to a neighboring tribe to seal a hasty alliance. When he brought his new bride to the bedchamber and eagerly removed her dress, he was shocked to discover a picture of his father and the words "limp-pricked whore monger" tattooed across her back. The alliance did not last very long.

Since that time, inks have been popular. Less durable, yes, but also less chance of making a permanent mistake. Through the use of this brush, warpaints can quickly be copied and used again.

<LoreItalics>Some gods are strong to harm, others, to aid; at least so say their priests.</> - Queen of the Black Coast

A spiritual residue left on religious altars

Over time, a place that is used for religious ceremonies takes on a certain significance. Not simply in the minds of the followers of that religion, but also in others who pass through an area.
In the oldest groves and shrines of the world, the presence of those ancient, gloomy gods can still be felt. In the shining altars of Mitra or the bloody slabs of Set, the manifestation of this spiritual presence is palpable.
When a shrine is defiled, this effect leeches slowly away, but if the defilers are of an opposing religion, they actually absorb the power that they have stolen. Thus altars are a precious commodity in the Exiled Lands and worship brings great bounties to those who pursue it.

Worshippers of Set are aware that displeasing their god can mean an altar and a blood drenched knife in their future. In order to keep the dictates of Set constantly on their minds, devotees place small statues around their dwellings to remind them of the precepts of the Old Serpent.

Few of the inhabitants of the Exiled Lands are lucky enough to sleep in a bed at night. Some disdain the comfort of a full bed, imagining that the softness of the mattress will cause a softening of their bodies and minds.
But some see the bed as a place of lovemaking, sleeping and dreaming. They consider it an important part of civilization and sneer at those who sleep on the ground as uncouth savages.
When somebody dies in the Exiled Lands, they awaken in the last place that they slept, unaware of how or why they got there. Using a bed will set it as your spawn point.
A folding bed that takes up little space

This bed made of leather stretched over a folding frame, take up less space than a conventional bed.
Commonly used in barracks, cheap inns and mercenary headquarters, this bed is valued mostly for its ability to be stacked and stored whenever it isn't being used.
When somebody dies in the Exiled Lands, they awaken in the last place that they slept, unaware of how or why they got there. Using a bed will set it as your spawn point until it is destroyed.
A low divan made in the Stygian style

Both couch and bed, the divan probably originated in Vendhya or Turan, but it rapidly became popular in the kingdom of Stygia. The most elaborate of divans are made of silk and gold inlaid ebony, but they can also be made from simple materials.
Stygian nobles are often portrayed as indolent and decadent and imagery of them lounging on divans, eating and drinking, has contributed to this portrayal. In practicality, during the hottest hours of the day all Stygians retire to their houses for leisure time and these rumors are probably spread by foreign merchants frustrated with a culture that doesn't follow their schedule.

A well that fills slowly over time

Made from rough stones and wood, this well manages to capture a small amount of water.
Water is an essential element for survival and this is doubly the case in the desert environments of the Exiled Lands. Any permanent settlement near water will inevitable be contested by others who also seek access to this life affirming resource.
The convenience of a well allows building in areas that would otherwise be unsustainable. Wells fill with water over time and can be used to quench thirst, replenish waterskins and perform the dozens of other activities that require the presence of water.

This opulent urn likely contains the ashes of nobility, a wealthy merchant, or prominent priest of Asura. There are some who believe that cremated ashes still contain power over the souls of the dead. To those believers, the ashes contained within the urn may hold more value than the urn itself.

<LoreItalics>His thirst allayed, he attacked the food before him with rare gusto. It too was strange to him: exotic fruits and unknown meats. The vessels were of exquisite workmanship, and there were golden knives and forks as well.' </>  - The Slithering Shadow

It's story has been lost to the passage of time.

Wind chimes crafted of human bones

The cannibal tribes of Darfar have developed a unique mechanism to warn them against the sandstorms that occasionally sweep through their lands. These wind chimes, made from the bones of humans, begin to chime when the wind picks up. If a sandstorm is coming, the noise of the chimes becomes impossible to ignore.
When the wind moves sluggishly through the Darfari camps, however, the chimes create an eerie, ghostly music. Perhaps this unsettling tune contributes to the unsettling reputation of the Darfari.

A low divan made in the Stygian style

Both couch and bed, the divan probably originated in Vendhya or Turan, but it rapidly became popular in the kingdom of Stygia. The most elaborate of divans are made of silk and gold inlaid ebony, but they can also be made from simple materials.
Stygian nobles are often portrayed as indolent and decadent and imagery of them lounging on divans, eating and drinking, has contributed to this portrayal. In practicality, during the hottest hours of the day all Stygians retire to their houses for leisure time and these rumors are probably spread by foreign merchants frustrated with a culture that doesn't follow their schedule.
When somebody dies in the Exiled Lands, they awaken in the last place that they slept, unaware of how or why they got there. Using a bed will set it as your spawn point until it is destroyed.

While individual Nordheimer clans may worship different minor deities, Ymir is considered the chief of all gods. The god of Storm and War is said to send his daughter Atali to fetch the souls of dead and dying warriors to fill the halls of Valhalla.

Made of woven camel-hair, these tents are deployed quickly and with little fuss and are actually quite a comfortable place to ride out a sandstorm.

Sandstorms in the Exiled Lands contain more than just wind-blown sand and flying fragments. There are darker terrors against which woven camelhair may not prove particularly effective.

Once a tent is placed, gaining shelter is a simple as crouching inside it.

Somewhere, far from the Exiled Lands, a scholar sits writing frantically. His master has given him the task of writing hundreds of descriptions of mundane items, from swords and armor, to plant fiber and stones. He glances at the next item on his list. Ladder. 

He stops, sets his quill down and looks at his reflection in a nearby mirror. He is a man grown old before his time, a slave in all but name to his masters. 

'What am I doing', he wonders. His life is a series of decisions that he almost didn't recognize that he was making.  As his thoughts spiral into the past and as he traces that inevitable trajectory backwards he realizes that there was no single point, no decision that brought him to this point. It was an accumulation of decisions across his entire lifespan, building around him like sand in the desert that leaves him living a life of quiet desperation, drowning slowly as the quicksand fills his throat.

As the realization hits him, he feels a vast sadness, an aching in his soul that he could have been so much more than simply this. A single, crystalline tear seeps from his eye and drips down onto the parchment he is working on, blurring the ink.

Resolving to make more of this life, the man stands, pushing aside his parchment, and moving to the door.

Which bursts open and, before the surprised scribe can even gasp, he is run through by a wild-eyed thief who has crept into the mansion in search of valuables.

The thief wipes his knife on the dead scholar's clothing, and glances around the room. His gaze wanders across the parchment on the table, filled with a list of items and descriptions written in the neat hand of the deceased scholar. He grins, and reaches for the quill.

Later, when the guards find the dead scholar, lying facefirst in a mingled pool of blood and ink, they will be briefly distracted by the bizarre message scratched into the parchment beside the word ladder. It simply reads: "Something you climb, idiot".

The guards shrug. Nobody really cares about the text anyway.

Originally created in Khitai for use in fireworks, enterprising warriors and merchants soon saw the value of using this explosive powder in warfare.
The jars are prepared, filled with the powder and carefully sealed against the air. The very touch of air is enough to ignite the powder yet each jar comes with a fuse that can be lit for a delayed detonation.

These traps were originally conceived by noblemen in Zingara to prevent human poachers from trespassing on their estate. The effectiveness of the traps was legendary and it wasn't very long until the traps were being used by hunters across the western kingdoms to capture animals.

This trap is only effective on players.
A pressure sensitive floor panel that releases sharpened spikes

<LoreItalics> Not the Grey Lotus, this time, but something just as effective. Nearly every chamber in my house is a trap.</> - Rogues in the House

Honest people defend their homes with stout walls and strength of arms. But devious people know that once a wall is breached, their enemy will be off guard. There are many traps that can be concealed within the walls and floor of a keep and thieves and conquerors alike would do well to keep their wits about them.

Nabonidus, the Red Priest, is rumoured to have filled his mansion with traps to kill the assassins and thieves which came to rob him of life and loot respectively. Ultimately they proved ineffective, as he was found murdered in his own mansion one morning, just inches from the trigger to one of his own traps.
A wooden trap for capturing small animals
This small trap is useful for capturing game and other small animals. It is not strong enough to keep anything larger than a rabbit pinned for very long.
A trap that releases a damaging vapor

Filled with a viscous, clinging vapor that eats the lungs and makes breathing impossible, this deadly trap is used by merchants in Zamora to discourage thieves. It is even proof against the sandstorm masks commonly crafted by desert tribesman to keep out sand particles - evidently the gas is able to seep into the masks regardless.
An exploding jar that can be buried

Originally created in Khitai for use in fireworks, enterprising warriors and merchants soon saw the value of using this explosive powder in warfare.
One enterprising Nemedian merchant thought that surrounding his mansion with a ring of explosive jars buried in the earth, their lids rigged with a special trigger, would deter would-be thieves from stealing over his walls. When his favorite hunting hound triggered the trap and knocked down half of the wall around his mansion, the merchant sold the details of the trigger mechanism to a blacksmith and left the estate behind.
A pleasure temple dedicated to the goddess Derketo

Derketo is a fertility goddess and she is worshipped for her ability to grant bounteous crops and good calving seasons. Her rituals, however, involved deviant orgies that can last for weeks and include necrophilia and bestiality.

Her places of worship are therefore chosen for comfort, style, and the freeing of inhibitions. They are places where life and death intertwine like a pair of lovers. Those who visit the pleasure places of Derketo are reminded what it is to live and die - and how pleasurable both can be.

A holy shrine dedicated to the worship of Mitra

Considered a good god, Mitra is worshipped throughout the Hyborian kings, replacing the worship of Bori from which those primitive tribes took their name.

Mitra's symbol is that of the phoenix, but when he is depicted it is in the form of a well built, bearded man. He abhors the bloody rituals of other religions and prefers for his followers to perform dignified, purification rituals.

Mitra's priests preach a monotheistic doctrine and as such their followers tend to persecute the members of other nearby religions. Due to this tendency, Chapels to Mitra cannot be built within a very long range of shrines to other gods.

The campfire is an adventurers best friend when the nights turn cold and the darkness presses in all around. Made from simple branches and twigs, the campfire is an excellent source of light and heat.

Campfires can be used to cook meat which is important given the number of parasites that infect the wild animals of the Exiled Lands. Better to eat some burned meat, than be poisoned for days.

With the light of a campfire, however, comes visibility. Wary travelers would do well to hide their fires, lest they be ambushed in the night by men with unsavory intentions.

<LoreItalics>They camped that night on the northern slopes of those hills, and hook-nosed, fiery-eyed men of the hill tribes came in scores to squat about the fires and repeat news that had come up out of the mysterious desert. </>- Black Colossus

This foundation is designed to be a reinforced base for building siege engines that require stability as they are fired.

Siege engines require immense amounts of labor to craft and maintain. They are expensive to transport, and the working parts break often, requiring constant supervision.

<LoreItalics>On the landward side mangonels rained boulders and tree-trunks among the defenders, shattering through roofs and crushing humans like beetles; rams pounded incessantly at the stones; sappers burrowed like moles in the earth, sinking their mines beneath the towers.</> - The Scarlet Citadel

This base piece of the trebuchet or ballista, once placed on a siege foundation, can be upgraded with a frame to reach full functionality.

In the so-called civilized kingdoms of Hyboria, nobles build great palaces with walls of mighty stone to protect themselves from their enemies at court and abroad. The solution to sturdy walls and cowardly nobility is the siege weapon. Machines of immense power, trebuchets and ballistas can hurl stones, corpses, and even specially designed explosives.

Their weakness is immobility. Once placed, they cannot be easily moved, and finding the correct range and angle requires time and patience. With repeated use, it is almost certain that some or all of the components of the siege weapon will degrade and need to be replaced.

<LoreItalics> 'All substance is one to him who holds the key of the cosmos,' he said cryptically. 'To an adept nothing is immutable. At will, steel blossoms bloom in unnamed gardens, or flower-swords flash in the moonlight.'</> - The People of the Black Circle

Fueled by the strange alloys of the Elder Races, this building serves as a convergence point in the untamed maelstrom that surrounds the Tower of Siptah. Its strange geometries and macabre angles betray a mathematical complexity unknown to most cultures of the Hyborian Age.

One does not need to understand, however, to replicate and the practical application of this building is that it may cloak a base from the creatures of the void or indeed - summon creatures from across the void to attack it.

A place to sell an animal to other players
The wealth of Hyborian nations is built upon the backs of their beasts of burden and those who know how to handle an animal. The sale of beasts is one of the foundations of the civilized world.
A map showing the ancient kingdom of the Giant-kings

This room is a copy of the maproom that exists beneath the Unnamed City. In times past, the Giant-kings used sorcery to quickly move their slaves around their kingdom, attuning their bracelets to different areas and then using the map room to get there.

While the terrain is slightly different, owing to the eons that have passed since the creation of the original map, this map room still retains the ability to quickly send anybody with a bracelet to one of the attuned obelisks.

It is speculated that in the dim past, the obelisks served as a form of permission for slaves - the more trusted the slave, the more access to obelisks. Now, it is simply a matter of finding them, wherever they are.
