Foundations should be the starting point for almost any structure. They provide stability to anything built atop them and prevent the growth of plants beneath them.
Placing a foundation is a significant act in the Exiled Lands. Once a foundation is placed by a clan or individual, that land is considered their territory. Nobody else may build in the immediate area, unless the foundation is destroyed.
Cobbled together from ill-fitting sandstone buttressed by flimsy branches scavenged from the environment, this is barely a step above rubble.
Despite its appearance, it will provide some protection from the elements and the predators that roam the Exiled Lands. Determined foes, however, will find it no barrier.

A ritual mask used by Darfari shamans to see the dead

Carved into solid wood and decorated with intricate symbols, the watcher mask is said to remove the veil between the wearer and the spiritual world where Yog dwells.
Darfari slaves, captured and carried into the Hyborian kingdoms do not have shamans of their own, and are forced to practise a perverted version of their religion. They have long since lost the art of creating masks such as these.
But in the southern deserts, darfari shamans practise a purer version of the religion. Through the aid of these masks they can see the dead and, it is rumored, manifestations of Yog himself.

This mask offers some protection from both weapons and the elements.

Shemitish turban commonly worn in the meadowland cities

The meadowland cities of western Shem thrive on the trade that comes with the caravans that pass into Turan and Khitai. Due to their access to these caravans, the Shemitish people often have access to the first pick of goods coming from the east - including fine silks from Khitai and brightly dyed cloth from Turan. This bounty of cloth is reflected in the loose fitting, comfortable clothing woven by the tailors of Shem.
This clothing is a practical bulwark against the elements but won't be enough to stop a blade.

A pair of bone earrings often worn by Vanir commoners

As the massive glaciers of the north expand and move southward, the kingdoms of Asgard and Vanaheim are pushed slowly southward. This, in part, contributes to the perception of the Vanir and Aesir as warlike people - they are continually looking to the south in search of new lands to settle. 

Thus not all Vanir that are encountered in the north are raiders and warriors, quite often the weary adventurer will stumble across a caravan of Vanir settlers, looking for fertile lands to settle their new clan.

These earrings provide no significant protection, but they are marked with clan symbols - so that if a dead settler is found, their possessions can be returned to the clan. Jokingly referred to by the Aesir as Vanearrings.

A headscarf popular among Zingaran Freebooters

The flamboyant Zingaran Freebooters are both loved and feared in their home nation. The naval rivalry between Argos and Zingara forms a platform for troubadours to spin tales of Zingaran chivalry on the high seas and romanticize the swashbuckling rogues who fight to preserve Zingaran honor.

Never mentioned are the screams of their victims, plucked from burning caravels to be sold in the slave markets of the south. Never mentioned are the sacked coastal towns and slaughtered villagers, left to rot among their broken homes.

Freebooters attire themselves in all manner of flamboyant outfits, but the headscarf is cheap, popular and practical.

The Relic Hunters of the Exiled Lands are a curious mix of mercenaries, thieves and desperate fools. They were the original group in the Exiled Lands, exhorted to come in search of great treasures in the ruins that dot the area.

The price of their admission was to wear a bracelet that ensured they could not run off with the treasures that they found.

This turban has been refined in the time that they have spent in the Exiled Lands, offering comfort against the warm weather of the region and limited protection against the scouring sands.

Historians link the rise and eventual fall of the Khari empire to its dominion over the slave trade. In fact, it's believed the Khari gained their reputation as master crafters through the careful theft and assimilation of knowledge held by those they enslaved.

When the inevitable occurred and slave turned against master, Khari survivors fled west to the desert where they encountered the last remaining vestiges of the serpent people. As devout worshippers of Set, the Khari venerated the serpent folk as living scions of their beloved reptile God and laid the foundations for the kingdom that would later be known as Stygia. What finally befell the Khari and their scaled patrons is lost to time.

Historians link the rise and eventual fall of the Khari empire to its dominion over the slave trade. In fact, it's believed the Khari gained their reputation as master crafters through the careful theft and assimilation of knowledge held by those they enslaved.

When the inevitable occurred and slave turned against master, Khari survivors fled west to the desert where they encountered the last remaining vestiges of the serpent people. As devout worshippers of Set, the Khari venerated the serpent folk as living scions of their beloved reptile God and laid the foundations for the kingdom that would later be known as Stygia. What finally befell the Khari and their scaled patrons is lost to time.

A mask that protects the weary traveller

<LoreItalics>I've been a mercenary captain, a corsair, a kozak, a penniless vagabond, a general -- hell, I've been everything except a king of a civilized country, and I may be that, before I die.</> - Beyond the Black River 

At first glance this mask seems like it could be found in any of a dozen cultures across the continent - but a closer inspection reveals a sinister aspect to the mask. On the inside, of the mask is a polished mirror - and when it is attached to the face one is instantly filled with a strange wanderlust. Strange dreams of foreign cities fill the mind, the contours and vistas of other lands and other worlds.  

When the mask is removed, there is a strange emptiness, as if the mask stole some of the dreams of the wearer and added them to its collection.
A tunic that protects the weary traveller

<LoreItalics>I've been a mercenary captain, a corsair, a kozak, a penniless vagabond, a general -- hell, I've been everything except a king of a civilized country, and I may be that, before I die.</> - Beyond the Black River 

At first glance this tunic seems like it could be found in any of a dozen cultures across the continent - but it is more comfortable than any such clothing has a right to be. 

It fits perfectly at first attempt - almost seeming to mold itself to the form of the wearer. When climbing, it never catches, never impedes. When swimming, it seems to swell with buoyancy, rather than dragging at the wearer in the way that regular clothing will. 

Whichever worlds this clothing passed through to finally make its way to the Voidforge at the base of Siptah's tower, it feels like it belongs here now.

An excerpt from Liu Fei's research journal

Day 178.

I find myself within the forest primeval - a trackless jungle wasteland stalked by antediluvian beasts from a lost age. Even the flora here evidences a malignant and threatening aspect.

Day 191.

At long last, I have discovered that which I seek. On the far edge of the jungle, I have identified a Yothga plant - a hell-spawned aberration of nature that should not be in our world.

While there is insufficient time to study the diabolic metaphysics of the Yothga, in simple terms, I believe the root system acts a dimensional conduit or gateway that will admit the demon to our world.

Day 192

Before I attempt to challenge the beast, I must gain power over it - I must learn its true name. Unfortunately, the only way to gain this hidden knowledge is from one of the demon's own ilk. Fortunately, demons are a treacherous and saturnine race, prone to betraying each other.

After the sun goes down, I will attempt contact with the demon world.
Liu Fei's Research Log Page 2 of 5
An excerpt from Liu Fei's research journal

Day 203

After eleven days of fevered meditation and fasting, I finally contacted a demon called Zalthiel. While I am certain Zalthiel was present on the very first night, it seems the beast saw fit to plague me with nightmares and waking visions of horror until it grew bored and wanted to see what I was about.

Day 204

Zalthiel demands I complete a series of trials to test my worth, but the demon is a trickster, and I must be wary. It withholds its secrets with a jealousy approaching that of the Silent Eunuch Order of Quang Ni - every tidbit of knowledge negotiated separately and carefully.

For each syllable of the name I seek, another task must be completed. The first challenge is to collect a dead man's last breath...

Day 208

After some trekking along the coastline, I found my opportunity with an unsuspecting band of pirates. Under the cover of darkness, I slipped through the shadows and abducted one of the drunken fools. I am sure he will not be missed.

Upon fulfilling this deed, Zalthiel granted me the first syllable: Me-
Liu Fei's Research Log Page 3 of 5
An excerpt from Liu Fei's research journal

Day 212

Zalthiel's second task finds me back at the jungle clearing where the blighted form of the Yothga grows. The demon bids me confront the plant to collect a jar of the intoxicating and corrupting cloud it emits.

Day 213

Today is a day of rest and healing.

Evading the lethal embrace of the Yothga required every ounce of my cunning and craft. It seemed the very air was charged with the plant's corrupting miasma, each breath of which, a step closer to madness.

Returning with the jar, the demon rewarded my perseverance with the second syllable: Zza.
Liu Fei's Research Log Page 4 of 5
An excerpt from Liu Fei's research journal

Day 214

For the third syllable, the demon demands the unthinkable.

I am instructed to capture specimens of a twisted and diabolical race of Imps, using a pound of my own skin as bait.

Perhaps my old master was right, and I do not possess the fortitude to serve the Celestial Emperor. I have failed. Unless--

Day 221

I have returned from my foraging mission into the heart of the jungle. There, deep within a cave did I find a rare mushroom variety that promises both the anesthetic and hallucinogenic properties I require to fulfill what is asked of me.

Day 222

The mushroom didn't work. The pain was excruciating as I flayed myself, every strip of flesh removed, a new and fresh agony.

But the Imps came, drawn to the enclosures by the scent of my flesh and blood.

For this, Zalthiel revealed the third syllable: Mal.

We've got ourselves a job, and it demands discretion. We're supposed to haul the blacksmith from his perch on the hill all the way to Stormwatch.

If he's not delivered in one piece we get no take, and there's enough gold in the pot for each of us to buy a seat on the high council. There's always a twist in jobs like these. The smith must be more than meets the eye for this great sum. Bring him in one piece cousin.

Take no risks. Avoid any suspicion that could tie this back to the clan.

Seeker of fortune,

I have a task that requires discretion. I would pay the sum of 300 gold pieces for the capture and safe delivery of the blacksmith Angvarr. He can be found at his hovel in the hills east of New Asagarth.

Bring him to me with no harm done and you will be rewarded handsomely. Should you maim or kill him, I'll ensure the molten gold lines your innards before you rot in a shallow grave.

The note is sealed in wax stamped with a raven's foot.

Fret not cousin. I'll pick up some Exile brutes to do the job with me. If there's anything they're good at, it's swinging a club. Once we return to Stormwatch, I'll gut the dogs. No one will miss them, and no one will know we were involved.
